items.quote: 007 First Light (o James Bond) me ha parecido un juegazo brutal y una experiencia súper disfrutable de principio a fin; para mí se lleva un 8,75 seguro. En general, casi todo en el juego es muy bueno. La historia te atrapa desde el primer minuto y se siente como estar viviendo una película de la franquicia, llena de escenas brutales que te dejan con la boca abierta. Además, está cargado de referencias a otras cosas y guiños al universo de Bond que los fans van a gozar muchísimo.A nivel técnico y artístico cumple con nota alta. Los gráficos son muy buenos y lucen espectaculares, acompañados de unas animaciones buenísimas que le dan mucho realismo a cada movimiento. El doblaje es genial y la música encaja a la perfección, elevando la tensión y la elegancia en los momentos clave. La duración también me ha parecido perfecta, dándote el tiempo justo para disfrutarlo sin que se sienta estirado. En lo jugable, el sistema de disparos está muy bien y funciona de locos, haciendo que los tiroteos sean súper satisfactorios. Además, lo combina genial con buenos puzles que le dan variedad y pausa a la acción. Por ponerle los únicos peros al juego: me falta un poco más de variedad de armas para poder experimentar con diferentes estilos. Y el punto flojo principal es la IA: los NPC a veces disparando se sienten un poco falsos y no reaccionan del todo bien, demostrando que la inteligencia artificial no está del todo bien trabajada. Pero quitando ese detalle de los enemigos, es un juego redondo, divertidísimo y completamente recomendado.

items.author: BitRaven

items.quote:
James Bond's Origin, the Scale, the gadgets, and galore make this game a narrative and enjoyable game to play all the way through.

IO Interactive put a lot of effort into this, and it shows.
Instead of ruining the experience that this game contains, and that feeling of being a spy, I'm just going to head right into the rating and explain why the rating is so.

Ratings:
Gameplay: 9/10, at first it's a little bit of a weird control scheme, but when you get used to it, the game, the gameplay, and everything feed into this high-action gameplay that responds to what you want to do.

Graphics: 8/10, It's great, but since the game isn't really optimized its difficult to play this at a good resolution and performance. RTX 3060 btw, more than enough power for AAA games.

Performance: 6/10, a combination of poorly implemented FSR and DLSS, coupled with DRM that will tank your system down to the 40s, at least for me.
But often I am reaching 60fps.

Music: 9/10, this is James Bond and the music fits every single chapter very well.

Story: 8/10, at the end it gets predictable, but as a newly founded James Bond fan, even I can tell you that the Ghost in the Wind is S P E C T R E. But they did make a compelling narrative with this game that takes heavy inspiration from the Uncharted Series.

Scummyness Meter. This game contains DENUVO DRM, isn't as optimised even for Consoles, and relies heavily on Upscaling. For this, I have to subtract 2 points in the performance section, 8 -> 6/10.

Overall, if I calculate my Rating together, 40/50 x 100, we get 80/100.
This game is very lucky indeed to get a total of 8/10 from me even with DRM and its performance; I did not encounter a single crash/game breaking bug.
The only thing I saw was the notifications showing the way was not correctly updated.

If and when IO remove the DRM and polishes the performance so it actually runs without upscaling, then this would be a 9/10. But for now, an 8/10 is in order.

I highly recommend this game as it tries something new with the 007 formula, while still retaining everything learnt from Hitman and drawing inspiration from the Uncharted games.

I look forward to the Sequel, and if it goes harder and longer than this game, we are in for a good time.

items.quote:
Not as good as the reviews make you believe. Enjoyably, but tedious at the end.

There's a lot going on with this title, both good and bad. First the good:
- lovely graphics
- runs well on an older pc (with Linux Mint and Proton Steam)
- nice bond-like humor and scenes
- very nice music
- pretty and different locations
- interesting story
- nice diversity of gadgets and going around things in the field (albeit very limited to only just that)
- nice build up of everything

And then there's the "bad" (my opinion)
- short
- very expensive for a short game like this
- controls (mouse keyboard) are "meh" and sometimes just frustrating when under pressure
- very scripted and linear: there really isn't any freedom and the game forces you through a mall,  The "freedom" is limited to gadget use, route through parkour area's and stealing cards/passes this way or the other, that's, for the rest you are playing in a movie.
- sometimes over the top and just not fun anymore, like going from a "trespassing area" to a complete hostile area with lots of fully armoured opponents,  to another "trespassing area" like nothing happened. or the scripted appearance of wave after wave of enemies from spots you cleared just a minute ago, or having to kill the same character over and over again, after having miraculously returned to life... you get the gist.
- not too likable characters. You are supposed to feel for them especially during the more emotional scenes, but yeah, this doesn't really happen because the connection and interactions between Bond and the others stays superficial, "rough and shallow" and don't develop one bit. 
- the end game was just boring and annoying. I found myself rushing the end just to get it over with.

So, in the end it was enjoyable, at times a bit cringy and frustrating, at other times I found myself laughing, but if you ask me if I'd recommend it, my final verdict would be "no". There are way better games available for this price.

items.quote:
General Assessment

To be honest, I have never played a Hitman game before, and when I learned that the same studio was developing 007: First Light, I was a bit hesitant because I didn’t have much interest in that genre. However, 007 managed to break that prejudice for me. I completed the game in a satisfying 18 hours on normal mode. The difficulty balance can be tricky; while it’s generally well-tuned, there are moments where it feels a bit off. The sense of freedom the game offers is quite sufficient, sometimes even bordering on excessive.

In-Depth Analysis

Learning the controls on PC was average. While the optimization is generally smooth, I experienced some performance stutters in certain areas using an RTX 3050. The unnecessarily long chapters and inconsistent pacing are the main downsides. Despite these flaws, it remains a creative and evolving game, thanks to its sandbox freedom, cinematic cutscenes, and innovative mechanics.

Final Verdict

I highly recommend getting this game. It is enjoyable, unique, and immersive—a title that truly makes you feel like James Bond and allows you to witness his evolution from start to finish. It’s a solid 7 to 7.5 out of 10 experience that leaves you with a very pleasant aftertaste.

items.quote: I just beat 007 First Light. Not too long, just took me 14 hours. I think the game is one of the best 007 games in a LONG TIME. Golden Eye on N64 was my last fond memory of a 007 game. The gameplay is basically a baby between Uncharted and Hitman. You have your action setpieces, your 3rd person cover shooter elements and your fist to fist combat. You have your occasional stealth segments and also your Hitman style stages which is no surprise as this is from the same developer. Those stages are a lot of fun because the aim is to get to a certain segment of the stage without getting caught. They always give you multiple ways to do this. For example, one stage you can find a way to steal a key from a security guard or brute force it by shooting a dart to make them sick or you can pretend to be a photographer so you can a press pass. The game also gives you a bluff system. You need to build up meter by stealth takedowns or such BUT once you build it up, you are allowed to bluff. It is basically a get out of jail card if you get caught during stealth or such which is a nice save to not ruin a stealth playthrough if you get accidentally caught. There are also classic 007 gadgets such as hacking, missile pen, dart phone, flash mine and shock wave camera. It's fun and incredibly creative.  The story is also very good. It's a reimagining of James Bond with it being an origin story of how he got the number which is unique. There is also a lot of great performances, Patrick Gibson is terrific as Bond, wonderful music score and beautiful locations and level design. I was shocked to see my home country of Vietnam in a game for once! It also explores A.I. in a fun interesting way. Everything with the writing here is the exact thing you would see in a 007 film!   If I do have any gripes, I guess there are some loose plot threads that are being obvious held for an eventual sequel. They even do a "James Bond will Return" text. What is this, Avengers Doomsday?? There are also some fun original supporting characters in the first third of the game that just dip from the story onwards which is a shame. I also wish there were more car chases because those are staples of 007 but there were surprisingly very little. Anyway, it was a fun game and I would love to see a sequel!

items.quote:
A highly cinematic and dynamic spy thriller that delivers the ultimate Bond fantasy, holding back from absolute masterpiece status only due to a dragging final act and heavily scripted chase sequences. 

On a technical level, the game is certainly demanding on hardware, but overall performance is solid. The experience runs smoothly without suffering from poor framerates, disruptive bugs, or glitches.

The game shines by encouraging a fluid mix of playstyles rather than forcing you down a strict action or stealth route. If you blow your cover, you can try talking your way out of the situation; if a shootout is inevitable, you can leverage environmental hazards like explosive barrels or use your watch to short-circuit your surroundings. The glaring mechanical flaw, however, lies in the driving and chase levels. They are heavily scripted, cinematic rollercoaster rides featuring excessive hand-holding where your inputs barely matter. I sincerely hope future iterations abandon these button-prompt sequences in favor of actual, interactive gameplay.

Artistically and narratively, the DNA of the 'Hitman trilogy' is evident in the world design and art direction, but it never detracts from the game's unique identity. As someone whose exposure was previously limited to Daniel Craig's films, I found this to be the perfect entry point. The game serves as an excellent introduction to the character; early training segments brilliantly establish the lore and world for newcomers. The story expertly delivers everything you expect from the franchise: scenic locations, beautiful women, tense investigations, double-crosses, and betrayals.

Holistically, this is easily the best James Bond experience I’ve ever had. The mechanics, narrative, and cinematic flair possess all the ingredients of a masterpiece, dragged down only by an uneven, weaker ending and pacing issues in the final chapters. Despite that, it is a phenomenal foundation and a genuinely great time.

James Bond 007: First Light est un jeu qui se situe à mi-chemin entre Hitman et Uncharted. Les différents décors sont variés, les séquences d'action sont dynamiques et les phases de gunfight se révèlent particulièrement plaisantes. Les nombreux gadgets enrichissent également le gameplay en offrant plusieurs façons d'aborder certaines situations. Du côté du scénario, l'ensemble est plaisant à suivre. L'histoire est rythmée par plusieurs rebondissements et reste extrêmement fidèle à l'univers de James Bond. Cependant, malgré ses qualités, je pense qu'il y avait matière à proposer une intrigue encore plus marquante et ambitieuse.

Malheureusement, le jeu souffre d'une certaine répétitivité dans ses phases d'investigation, qui peuvent devenir lassantes à la longue. Certains gadgets manquent aussi d'ergonomie et ne sont pas toujours agréables à utiliser.

Malgré ces défauts, j'ai particulièrement apprécié le système de chapitrage qui multiplie les références aux films de la saga James Bond, renforçant l'immersion pour les fans de la licence.

Au final, James Bond 007: First Light est une aventure divertissante qui séduira surtout les amateurs de l'agent secret britannique.

items.quote:
007 First Light is a stealth/action game.

You play as a young James Bond, the game starting out even before you become a 00 agent, on a mission where you end up attracting the attention of MI6 as a potential operative. You go through a training montage, training with other prospective 00 agents, and build some bonds with them, as well as your instructor, Greenway, who is a former 00 agent himself.

Of course, the game would not be a James Bond story if there weren’t twists and turns, and the game has a good number of plot twists. The obvious villain at the start of the game isn’t the main villain (though the actual main villain is not exactly subtle), and the game manages to take you through a variety of different locations and scenarios as you try and resolve the current crisis. It has a number of fun setpieces and you have to infiltrate a bunch of different places over the course of the story, with segments shifting between stealth, puzzle solving in more socially mingling environments, and gunplay segments where you have to blast your way through enemies and drive vehicles on chases.

The game thus alternates between these different modes to try and keep things fresh and varied, and while it works well from the perspective of mixing things up, unfortunately, it is also where the game falls down hardest.

The core of the problem is that none of these segments are particularly good – the driving is lackluster, the social mingling is decent but ends up being a bit samey over time, the stealth mechanics are pretty much the same throughout the game (use something to distract the person -> sneak past them), and the gunplay is pretty basic and repetitive, without much variety in enemies. There are a few things that mix up the gameplay a bit more, but all in all, the gameplay is really the weakest part of this game – it ends up feeling repetitive by the end of it because there just isn’t enough depth to any of the game’s mechanics.

Story-wise, the story is solid enough, with fun, well-acted characters (both friend and foe) and an overall solid enough plot. James Bond is likeable, and is a bit impetuous and independent here, showing a stubborn streak. He works well enough, and the implication that there were other 00s before him (along with various easter egg references to movies/stories) is fun. Moneypenny, Q, M, Greenway, your fellow 00 recruits, and some other friends and foes are fun enough characters, and work pretty well all told.

Overall, I think this game is pretty decent, and I feel like this game does a much better job of “making you feel like James Bond” than any other 007 game ever has; this game has a lot more actual spying going on, with you engaging in social interactions and “hiding in plain sight” rather than having to sneak through every area behind waist-high walls or just blast your way through everything.

But I think the game mechanics’ shallowness holds the game back from absolute greatness.

items.author: Shoei

items.quote:
1. GAMEPLAY REVIEW
In this section the focus is on the gameplay mechanics, it provides the elements that are standard for a title in the James Bond series, including a protagonist with a strong presence and a narrative that generates interest. To complete objectives, the player uses specialized electronic and mechanical tools.
But the stealth systems are particularly prominent, those mechanics share many structural attributes with the Hitman series, which serves the needs of players who prefer strategic movement. At the beginning of development, there was a concern that the developers would only change the appearance of the Agent 47 character. By choosing a different path, however, the studio created a product that is more distinctive and focuses more on the motivations of the characters.
As for the combat design, it functions through a system that allows for various methods of completion. If a player prefers to move without being seen, they use the shadows, the surroundings and false clothing. And if a player chooses to abandon secrecy, the system allows for forceful and audible neutralizations. With this design the player decides the specific manner in which they finish a task.
For many players the bluffing system is a significant addition. It is possible to use dialogue to escape a situation where enemies are suspicious. By using those verbal interactions, the player influences enemies to enter secure zones or moves them into positions where they are vulnerable to a physical strike.
Then again the game is not without faults, if there is a primary criticism of the experience, it is the sections involving vehicles. The operation of the cars is slow and repetitive. It does not provide the high level of excitement that is common during a James Bond vehicle pursuit.
GAMEPLAY SCORE: 8.5 / 10.

2. STORY REVIEW
It is positive that the story does not function as a low quality product that depends on memories of previous movies. By doing the necessary work, IO Interactive provides an original story about the character when he is young.
As a person who likes the films, I saw that the developers managed the character of Bond well. He displays a specific type of male presence that is similar to the versions played by Daniel Craig besides Pierce Brosnan. He is likeable but also poses a threat to others. With this writing, the game shows that he is susceptible to harm while he remains calm and composed. Because of this approach, the events in the story affect him in a private way. When the game ends, the plot is interesting enough that a player might feel a sense of sadness because the experience is over. For many there is a desire for more chapters to be available to play.
STORY SCORE: 8 / 10.

3. PERFORMANCE REVIEW
For the majority of the time, First Light operates without significant errors. It is common for the motion to be fluid and the number of frames displayed per second remained consistent during the period of play.
However, it definitely needs a few patches. In some sessions the program stopped responding entirely, which made it necessary to return to the system menu and initiate the game again. When the display contains many moving elements like explosions or large numbers of opponents, the frames per second are lower than usual, those events are not frequent enough to prevent progress and the system creates save points often so that players do not lose much progress. On the whole the game is stable.
PERFORMANCE SCORE: 8 / 10.

5. GRAPHICS & VISUALS REVIEW
On the subject of the visual presentation, the game contains high quality graphics. As traveling across the world is a significant element of the James Bond genre, First Light represents this accurately. To play the game involves moving between locations that are visually impressive and the team that created the environment art produced high quality work. The views are wide and detailed. When missions occur at night, the lighting mimics the way light behaves in the real world. Because the graphics are detailed, the experience is more intense for the player. It is pleasant to explore the levels because they have many small details.
GRAPHICS & VISUALS SCORE: 8.5 / 10.

OVERALL SCORE 8.5 / 10.

items.quote: I played Hitman before; it was hard but fun, so I decided to give this game a try. I know James Bond but have never really watched any of the movies, so this is my first introduction to him, and it's great. The British accent, personality and quips make him a likeable character. The game is fantastic; the multiple choices of progression and enemy takedown are amazing. The gadget is intuitive and makes the game so much fun. The dialogue and voice acting are great. The outfit and location are beautiful. But the star for me is the stealth gameplay; the fact that you need to eavesdrop to collect information and then use gadgets to progress while also having the option to improvise is a different experience. I just wish there were a quick save because I keep restarting my game so I can do a perfect run of my plan. The story is great; it starts slow, but when everything starts to make sense, it becomes better, exploring different places and trying to do the right thing. The villain I thought was just normal at first, so whatever, but then they started to become more quirky with the AI brain tech and super suit; it's cool. The driving is better than I expect. Some characters are alright, but most are amazing. Nevertheless, the controller controls in combat are horrid; they're slow, and aim assist is not helping. I always find myself using the keyboard in a gunfight because the gunfight in this game is fast-paced, which is good but not if you're using a controller. The headshots are satisfying, though. The crouch controls are confusing, like I don't understand why the dashes are so weird and why sometimes we clip to the back of a blockage and sometimes not. Overall it was quite a journey; looking forward to more.

items.quote: When this was announced, I wasn’t sure what to make of it. I love IOI, as those Hitman games are incredible, but the worst part of those games is the shooting. I was worried that the gunplay wouldn’t be great here as well as the hand to hand stuff, as Hitman doesn’t really deal with that in a significant way. But, after seeing gameplay a few months before release, I was sold. And after playing it, I am not sure what I was worried about in the first place. These guys just know how to make great games. You get all that great Hitman DNA into a spy thriller and it is hitting on all cylinders. The combat is super fun, the animations on everything is top notch, the environments are a step above even the great Hitman stages. The characters and dialog is also pretty great, it looks and sounds exactly how you want it, like a Bond movie. From the score to the locations to the wardrobe, it is all **** even have vehicle segments, which are a must have if you want to be like the films. Now, after playing a lot of Forza Horizon 6, the cars here don’t feel as good (obviously), but for the small sections you have them, they control fine. The endgame Tactical Sim stuff is also really cool and that stuff is just straight up Hitman style. Although, it would be cool if they opened up some of their bigger levels for these modes as well. It looks like they will be supporting that mode for a long time, so more stuff with existing assets should be coming. It also really nails what it is going for and I am 100% there for the next one as well. This is far and away the best 007 game ever made and it isn’t even close. I mean, I know they haven’t made one in quite awhile, but this is still on top even the nostalgia people still have for the overrated N64 title. I will say the one questionable part of this game is the story. The overall story is good, but there are a few plot points it just completely ignores that you never get closure on and that really ****. It took me a day or two after finishing it to realize it as well, like “Oh, yea what ever happened to that guy?, etc.”. I still highly recommend it.

items.quote: This is the closest experience you can get to Uncharted, a First Light-style game that feels like a journey of creating the legendary agent James Bond. You see him as a reckless, impulsive young man who struggles to follow orders and slowly learns the consequences of his lack of discipline, which made me more attached to his character over time.What really stood out is that the game doesn’t treat Bond like a Terminator or Rambo. You’re a secret agent, not just a fighter. The game isn’t about constant shooting and explosions; instead, you truly live the role of a spy through stealth, infiltration, and multiple mission **** game rewards intelligence over chaos. Sometimes you get a notification saying you are authorized to kill, and at that point everything turns into controlled chaos where you mix tools and weapons—hacking devices, distracting enemies, luring one, throwing another into a wall, exploding this and killing that. It becomes a highly satisfying action **** game feels like a movie. There are intense encounters, car chases, and many unexpected twists. Not everything goes as expected, and the story keeps you engaged with surprises and complications. Bond himself is a likable, intelligent, and stylish character who constantly drags you into chaos and chases, similar to Uncharted vibes.Voice acting is strong, visuals are solid, and performance is smooth. However, the pacing can sometimes feel slow, AI behavior for NPCs can be a bit dumb at times, and unfortunately there is no Arabic translation despite it being a story-driven game that depends heavily on subtitles.Overall, the game delivers an enjoyable spy experience worthy of James Bond’s name.Final rating: 8.7/10

items.quote:
“Expect the Unexpected”

At first, 007 First Light feels like a fairly standard 7/10 action game. It lacks some of the creativity that IO Interactive brought to the recent Hitman trilogy, often guiding the player through smaller levels with limited freedom. Clear yellow and blue environmental markers frequently direct your path, reducing opportunities for exploration and problem-solving. The opening hours also suffer from some strange pacing and a few predictable plot points, leaving me concerned that I was playing a linear Xbox 360-era single-player game with a modern facelift.

However, the more you embrace IO’s vision for Bond, the more the game begins to shine. Rather than attempting to recreate Hitman, the developers lean heavily into the blockbuster spy thriller experience while sprinkling in enough stealth and player freedom to remind you of their previous work. As the story progresses, the game sweeps you along with its action, spectacle, and unmistakable Bond atmosphere.While the story initially feels cheesy and predictable, it quickly reveals several genuinely strong twists backed by excellent performances. Bond himself is particularly well cast. Despite this being a younger version of the character, he never stops feeling like James Bond.

IO has also included several classic Bond-style driving sequences. While they’re enjoyable, I would have liked at least one more iconic Aston Martin moment. It’s clear that driving gameplay isn’t the studio’s strongest area, but they’ve laid a solid foundation to build upon in future titles.

Combat and stealth feel much closer to Batman: Arkham and Uncharted, with basic countering, parrying, and melee combat. The hand-to-hand combat is weighty, the finishers are satisfying, and the game does an excellent job of making you feel like an elite, almost unstoppable spy. The gadgets in the game certainly aren’t groundbreaking, and most are introduced early on. The main fun comes from interacting with the environment to creatively neutralise your enemies.

There isn’t as much replayability compared to the Hitman games, but with challenges, collectibles, and Tact Sims, it’s clear IO is supporting replayability while already showcasing future Tact Sim missions. Tact Sims are mini challenge levels based on areas from the campaign missions, which become increasingly challenging as more restrictions are put in place.

Overall, there is little doubt in my mind that this is the best Bond game ever made. More importantly, it feels like the beginning of something special. IO Interactive has created strong foundations for what could have been an unforgettable Bond trilogy. The game is packed with references for long-time fans, and by the end, you’ll likely be eager to see more of this new interpretation of Bond.

The disappointment comes from the recent news that Amazon will be taking control of the franchise. After such a promising start, it’s difficult not to wonder what IO could have achieved with a full trilogy. Personally, I would have preferred to see them continue their vision for the series, and I hope Amazon sticks with IO.
As a Brit, I’ll happily say, keep the Danes in charge of Bond games. 

If you love James Bond and enjoy cinematic, story-driven action games with light stealth elements, excellent performances, and plenty of spectacle, 007 First Light is well worth your time. It may not reinvent the genre, but it delivers an entertaining spy thriller from start to finish.

And that shift in thinking is what makes this feel genuinely **** mission structure respects your intelligence. Every objective has multiple approaches — your discovery, your playstyle, your call. I played on the hardest difficulty and died often, but it never felt unfair. It felt like the game was teaching me something. The training sessions, which are easy to overlook, are worth every minute — they prepare you for real missions in ways the main game alone **** story keeps you guessing without cheap twists. Patrick Gibson, who I doubted from the trailer alone, delivers a performance that only makes sense in motion. He was the right choice. 007 First Light has genuine Game of the Year potential. Not because it's the loudest game of the year. Because it's one of the most thoughtful ones.

items.quote: I went into this wanting to like it. I've played plenty of modern games this year that I thought were just "okay" despite seeing their potential. Unfortunately, 007 First Light isn't one of those cases. My biggest issue is that it barely feels like a game. The experience is heavily focused on cutscenes, dialogue, scripted sequences, and slowly walking from one objective to the next. Large portions of the game feel more like an interactive movie than a traditional action or stealth title. There were long stretches where I felt like I was simply holding forward while characters talked, waiting for the game to let me actually play again. The marketing and developer pedigree might make you expect something closer to Hitman, but don't go in expecting that level of player freedom. Most missions are extremely linear and often provide only the illusion of choice. Even when you're given multiple ways to approach a situation, the outcome is usually heavily scripted. The game constantly funnels you toward a single intended solution, which makes experimentation feel **** stealth mechanics are incredibly forgiving. Enemy AI is easy to exploit, gadgets feel underutilized, and there is very little challenge on normal difficulty. Combat isn't much better. The melee system feels janky, inconsistent, and lacks the polish you'd expect from a major AAA release. Several encounters felt less like they were testing my skill and more like I was wrestling with the controls and **** story also failed to hold my attention. While there are a few interesting ideas, the dialogue is forgettable, several plot points feel underdeveloped, and most of the cast left little impression on me. As an origin story for James Bond, it never really captured the charisma, confidence, or excitement that I associate with the character. Bond spends much of the game reacting to events rather than driving them, which makes him feel surprisingly passive for a franchise built around one of fiction's most iconic action heroes.Another issue is pacing. The game spends a significant amount of time on tutorials, scripted story moments, and sequences that don't meaningfully develop either the gameplay or narrative. By the end, I felt like the game had far less actual gameplay than its runtime would suggest. What disappoints me most is that this game had all the ingredients to be great: a legendary franchise, a large budget, and developers with experience making stealth games. Instead, it feels like another example of a modern AAA title prioritizing cinematic presentation over meaningful gameplay. The production values are undeniably high, but impressive visuals and expensive cutscenes can only carry an experience so far.I also don't see much reason to replay it. Since the missions are so heavily scripted and player choice is limited, there isn't much incentive to return once you've seen the story play out. If you're looking for a story-driven interactive movie, you may enjoy it. If you're looking for a deep stealth game, a satisfying action game, or something that captures the spirit of classic Bond adventures, I found it hard to recommend.

Resumo:Após 6 horas de jogo, 007: First Light se consolida como uma experiência de ação extremamente polida e imersiva. A execução é exemplar, rivalizando com o nível de qualidade narrativa e de produção de títulos como The Last of Us Part II. items.quote: This might be one of the best action adventure games I've ever played. A straight 10/10 experience from beginning to end. 007 First Light doesn't just capture what makes James Bond special, it fully embraces it and delivers the ultimate interactive Bond fantasy. From the opening mission to the final credits, I felt like I was starring in my own blockbuster spy film. The gameplay is where this game truly shines. The developers somehow managed to combine the best elements of Hitman and Uncharted into one seamless experience. On one hand, you have the freedom and creativity of a spy thriller where planning, infiltration, and stealth are rewarded. On the other hand, you have the cinematic set pieces, action sequences, and thrilling escapes that make every mission feel like it belongs in a Bond movie. What I loved most was the freedom of choice. Nearly every situation allows you to decide how you want to approach it. You can sneak through an area unnoticed, carefully taking down enemies and gathering intelligence. You can go in guns blazing and rely on your shooting skills to survive. Or you can mix both approaches together depending on how the mission unfolds. The game never forces you into a single playstyle, and that flexibility makes every mission feel exciting and replayable. The combat and fighting mechanics are also fantastic. Whether you're exchanging gunfire, engaging in hand to hand combat, or improvising during intense encounters, everything feels fluid and satisfying. The melee combat especially stood out to me because it feels impactful and cinematic without becoming repetitive. Every fight feels like something straight out of a James Bond film. The presentation is absolutely top tier. The visuals are stunning, the locations are breathtaking, and every mission feels larger than life. From glamorous high society events to dangerous enemy strongholds, the game constantly puts you in iconic Bond situations. The attention to detail is incredible, and the world feels authentic from beginning to end. The story is exactly what I wanted from a James Bond game. It delivers espionage, action, intrigue, betrayal, and memorable characters while maintaining the sophisticated charm that defines the franchise. It strikes the perfect balance between being a thrilling spy adventure and a personal journey for Bond himself. And I have to give special recognition to Lana Del Rey because she absolutely nailed the theme song. Her voice perfectly captures the elegance, mystery, and emotion that have always defined the best Bond themes. The song instantly felt iconic, and honestly, I'd love to hear her contribute to more movies in the future because she was the perfect choice for this soundtrack. What impressed me most is how cinematic the entire experience feels. Every mission, every action sequence, every conversation, and every set piece feels like you're playing through a major Hollywood production. It never loses sight of what makes James Bond special, and because of that, it succeeds on every level. It's rare for a game to perfectly blend action, stealth, storytelling, freedom of choice, and cinematic presentation, but 007 First Light somehow accomplishes all of it. For me, this isn't just a great James Bond game, it's one of the best action adventure games ever made.

items.quote: Here is the shortened and summarized version of your review:### Review: 007 First Light (Shortened)I finished the game in about 15 hours on Normal difficulty. Developed by the creators of *Hitman*, it plays like a fantastic blend of *Hitman* and *Uncharted*, perfectly capturing the origin story of James Bond.**The Pros:*** **The "Bluff" Feature:** A brilliant and innovative addition to stealth gameplay.* **Combat & Gunplay:** Excellent hand-to-hand combat and satisfying shooting mechanics.* **Weapon Throwing:** Throwing an empty gun at an enemy's head is incredibly fun and useful.* **Level Design & Story:** Great episodic map changes and a compelling "rookie to 007" character arc.**Neutral:*** **Enemy AI:** It can be inconsistent; sometimes enemies act clueless even when you are right next to them.**The Cons:*** **Driving:** The vehicle mechanics are clunky and unenjoyable.* **Repetitiveness:** Dialogue and mission structures (like stealing keycards) get a bit repetitive later in the game.* **Missing Stealth Features:** The lack of body-hiding and disguises feels like a missed opportunity.* **Limited Arsenal:** There is a lack of weapon/gadget variety, and ammo limits feel too restrictive for an action game.### The Bottom Line**007 First Light** is a gripping 15-hour experience that brilliantly balances stealth and action while exploring a young James Bond's journey. Despite some minor repetitive elements and missing mechanics, the combat, story, and overall gameplay hook you right until the end. I highly **RECOMMEND** it!

items.quote:
Note: This is written from the perspective of someone who LOVES the Hitman WOA games.

Reviews for this game are weirdly polarised, but ignore those—it's really an OK game with some strengths and some weaknesses. I enjoyed it overall, but won't be spending much more time with it after finishing the main story.

Strengths:
- Absolutely phenomenal presentation aesthetically
- Engrossing story (with just one or two clunky moments)
- Well-optimised PC performance

Weaknesses:
- Tries so hard to be a movie, it fails to be a game—half the time feels like a walking simulator
- Tied in with the above, weird pacing—tries relentlessly to keep flowing into the next sequence, as though it expects you to play through the whole game in a single sitting, but it's a 15-20 h game, not a 2h movie!

Both stealth and combat are relatively unfun—many of us can't help comparing this to the phenomenal Hitman 2016+ series IOI developed beforehand, and it's a significant downgrade in gameplay:
- Open-ended puzzle-solving has been replaced with handholdy walking simulator type situations. 
- The simple but well-tuned gunplay has been converted into what I felt was an overcomplicated mix of melee and shooting. 
- Hitman's mix of movement and disguise-based stealth has been replaced by gadget-based (and dialog-based) stealth that again feels overcomplicated but at the same time repetitive to me personally.
- Movement in Hitman was effortless and responsive; here, agent 007 feels clunky to control and occasionally refuses to move the direction I press, which was frustrating

IOI has clearly tried to outdo Naughty Dog's Uncharted and the Last of Us in creating a story-rich experience, but unfortunately at the cost of gameplay and pacing. Overall, worth playing if you like action games, but maybe not at full price, and maybe not if you're too busy for games that are 'good' but not 'great'.

items.quote:
No começo eu estava bem ansioso, pois era um novo jogo do James Bond. Minhas expectativas estavam bem baixas, mas que surpresa incrível!

Depois das primeiras horas, o jogo simplesmente me conquistou de vez. É James Bond de verdade, senhores! Aquela sensação autêntica de ser o maior agente secreto do mundo, com muito estilo, charme, elegância e ação empolgante. Dirigir carros icônicos, usar gadgets, infiltrar-se em locais perigosos e partir para a ação quando necessário... o jogo captura perfeitamente a essência de 007. Fiquei completamente viciado!

As mecânicas estão excelentes. O combate corpo a corpo é fluido, impactante e extremamente satisfatório, com animações ótimas. A mistura de stealth com tiroteios funciona muito bem, dando várias opções de abordagem em cada missão. O gameplay é dinâmico, envolvente e te faz sentir poderoso como o próprio Bond.

Tecnicamente, o jogo me impressionou bastante. Roda de forma bem estável e, mesmo no médio, os gráficos estão lindíssimos. Os cenários são ricos em detalhes, a iluminação é fantástica e tudo transmite uma vibe cinematográfica de filme de 007. Parabéns à IO Interactive! Esse foi meu primeiro jogo deles e saí impressionado com a qualidade do trabalho. Virei fã na hora.

Já estou com 21 horas de jogo e estou perto de finalizar. Sinceramente, eu queria muito mais horas hahaha. Achei esse jogo tão bom que fiquei com gostinho de quero mais o tempo todo. Tomara que, em uma sequência, eles aumentem bastante a duração da campanha, porque o potencial aqui é enorme.

Resumindo: 007 First Light é sensacional! Um dos melhores jogos de ação e espionagem dos últimos tempos. Se você é fã de James Bond ou gosta de jogos com ótima história, stealth e combate empolgante, não pode deixar passar. Mal posso esperar pelas continuações. License to thrill ativada!

items.quote: First Light 007 is a magnificent gaming experience that completely immerses you in the thick atmosphere of a true spy thriller right from the very first minutes. The developers have managed to create an incredibly cinematic product where you genuinely feel like the main character of a big-budget secret agent movie. The gameplay is crafted beautifully, and the feature built around constant interaction with a gadget is executed brilliantly. It is not just a cosmetic prop, but a fully realized and engaging mechanic that drives plenty of cool scenarios. The graphics and visuals are a treat for the eyes, but the stunningly realistic mirrors deserve a special mention—proper reflections are hard to come by in modern games, and here, this detail works perfectly for total immersion. You sincerely believe in the characters thanks to the excellent acting, while the well-timed humor beautifully breaks up the tense moments, keeping the game from sliding into excessive pathos. If you love the spy aesthetic, quality directing, and clever gameplay, you definitely shouldn't pass this up; the game deserves the highest praise

items.quote: My experience with 007 First Light was a huge disappointment, turning what should have been a grand secret agent adventure into a complete technical and ergonomic nightmare. Right from the start, the game showed its limits with a sloppy level of polish, highlighted by major bugs like a total crash during the opening cinematic. My progress quickly hit broken scripts, particularly during the training sessions in Q's lab where targets failed to respawn, completely trapping me in the area and forcing me to reload my save. On top of that, the objective guidance is disastrous, forcing me to wander aimlessly just to find absurd narrative triggers like a broken phone hidden in a restroom, while the endless load times after every death finished off whatever patience I had **** terms of gameplay, the title markets itself as a modern experience when it actually delivers archaic and ultra-rigid stealth. Far from the freedom I expect from a Hitman game, it locks me into strict corridors. The artificial intelligence relies on stationary guards with overlapping lines of sight straight out **** from fifteen years ago, making even the slightest attempt at improvisation instantly punitive. This rigidity extends to my character's movement, as he is unable to jump or crawl under obstacles during the boat sequence unless prompted by a contextual action, while the climbing phases are fully automated and utterly **** action sequences fail to save the experience and proved to be just as frustrating. Gunfights boil down to pushing through brutal walls of bullets where I die in seconds, made worse by a ridiculous scarcity of ammunition that forces me to constantly scavenge corpses, along with an absurd "permission to fire" mechanic. Hand-to-hand combat is heavy, clunky, and imprecise, leaving me running around in a panic looking for any random object to throw at enemies. As for my gadget arsenal, my secret agent fantasy was **** by the ridiculous requirement to rummage through trash cans and drawers for batteries or chemicals—an artificial looting mechanic designed solely to limit my gear and force me into using the Bluff system, a tedious dialogue mini-game that destroys the pace of the **** immersion was further ruined by an unlikable cast and setting. The writing turns MI6 into a toxic workplace where my boss, M, spends his time barking orders and belittling me over the comms, while Moneypenny loses all her charm to become an annoying nag. Even the vehicle sequences, which should be a staple of the franchise, suffer from a complete lack of feedback and are an absolute **** breaking point came during the warehouse sequence. Pinned down under relentless enemy fire, given no clear direction, and worn out by my character repeating the exact same hint line on a loop, I simply had enough. This accumulation of poor design, constant frustration, and outdated mechanics wrapped in empty marketing hype made my decision easy: I quit the game on the spot and permanently uninstalled a title that has nothing to offer beyond an empty marketing shell.

items.quote: I played James Bond First Light on PlayStation 5 Pro, and as someone who has always enjoyed the James Bond franchise, both through the classic films and most of the video games, I had a really good time with **** has been a long time since we had a proper James Bond video game, and First Light does a good job of bringing back the feeling of the franchise. The story uses many of the classic Bond ingredients: conspiracies, betrayals, high-level tension within MI6, varied missions and a strong spy atmosphere. At times, it really feels like playing through an interactive Bond movie, which works very well for this kind of **** gameplay feels natural and enjoyable. The game moves between platforming, stealth, action and driving sequences, which keeps the pacing fresh. The vehicle sections are also quite fun and add some welcome variety. I liked the way the game constantly switches between different types of gameplay while still feeling coherent.Visually, the game is more uneven. Some scenes look really good, with nice environments and strong cinematic direction. However, there is also some clipping, textures sometimes appear late, and a few visual details lack polish. It is not a major issue, but it does prevent the game from feeling technically excellent.I finished the game over a few evenings, playing sessions of around one and a half to two hours, and I genuinely enjoyed the experience. It is a fully single-player, cinematic adventure, and honestly, it feels good to play something like this without competition, online pressure or multiplayer systems.That being said, replay value is quite limited. Once finished, I did not really feel a strong reason to start it again immediately. It is more the kind of game you may replay years later with some nostalgia, like rewatching a good action **** is not game of the year material, but it is a very enjoyable experience and a successful tribute to the James Bond franchise. A solid and entertaining return for Bond in video game form.

items.author: ob

items.quote:
Hier ist die nochmals feingeschliffene Fassung. Ich habe die Kritik an der fehlenden deutschen Sprachausgabe (und den damit verbundenen Untertiteln im Gameplay) nahtlos in den Block zur Inszenierung und Atmosphäre eingebaut:
Rezension: [007 First light] – Ein starkes Fundament mit Agentenschwächen
Eine wirklich schöne Story, die sich hervorragend in das bekannte 007-Universum einbettet. Man lernt zusammen mit Bond die typischen Aufgaben, Kniffe und Mechaniken seiner Spionage-Karriere von der Pike auf kennen. Getragen wird das Ganze von einer fantastischen Grafik und einer dichten, eleganten Inszenierung, die den Geist der Filme perfekt einfängt – vom exzellenten Sounddesign bis hin zu den detailverliebten, luxuriösen Schauplätzen. Auch das Pacing zwischen ruhigen Schleichpassagen und packenden Sequenzen stimmt. Ein Wermutstropfen für die Atmosphäre ist allerdings das komplette Fehlen einer deutschen Sprachausgabe. Wer der englischen Sprache nicht absolut mächtig ist, muss permanent Untertitel mitlesen, was gerade in dynamischen Gameplay-Momenten ablenkt und der filmischen Immersion schadet.
Abzüge gibt es zudem bei der Inszenierung der Action. Die KI ist schlicht zu einfach gestrickt und agiert in Schusswechseln oft kopflos. Zudem wirken die Schusssequenzen durch die allzu plump und auffällig platzierten roten Fässer oder freiliegenden Leitungen arg konstruiert. Hier fehlt es dem Spieldesign an Subtilität; die Umgebungen schreien dem Spieler die Interaktionsmöglichkeiten förmlich entgegen, statt zum cleveren Experimentieren einzuladen.
Die unverkennbaren Hitman-Wurzeln der Entwickler sind spürbar, wurden hier jedoch spürbar vereinfacht. Das tut dem Spielfluss grundsätzlich gut, da es den Fokus weg vom reinen Sandbox-Puzzle hin zu einer geradlinigeren Agenten-Erfahrung verlagert und dem Spiel eine eigene Identität verleiht. Gelegentlich führt diese Vereinfachung aber auch zu einem recht starren Leveldesign, das einem wenig kreativen Spielraum lässt. Während die Umgebungen optisch glänzen, wirken manche Charakteranimationen in den Cutscenes zudem etwas hölzern.
Die Eskalationsmissionen sind eine nette Dreingabe für zwischendurch, fallen vom Umfang her aber noch viel zu gering aus. Auch das Missionsdesign **** hier: Einige spielerische Ideen und Aufgaben sind durchaus interessant, andere wiederum wirken eher bemüht oder gar blöd gelöst.
Fazit: Das spielerische und atmosphärische Fundament steht. Wenn das Team für den Nachfolger die KI anzieht, die Umgebungsrätsel subtiler gestaltet, eine vollständige Lokalisierung spendiert und den Mut zu mehr spielerischer Freiheit hat, erwartet uns ein absolutes Highlight. Ich bin definitiv gespannt, was das Team aus Teil 2 macht.

items.quote: I have not been so invested in a 007 game since Agent Under Fire and GoldenEye, but this? This just does it for me. This isn't just a game. This is 007. This is James Bond. YOU are James Bond. The agent. The playboy. The debonair. Many games go for that "feels-like-a-movie" vibe, but IO Interactive puts on a master class performance with this production.  Celebrity cameos from Gemma Chan, Kenny Kravitz, etc., immaculate world building taking you on an international espionage-laced journey, beautiful women, beautiful set pieces, iconic gadgets, nods to cinema, the Lana Del Rey opening number, etc. Everything about 007 First Light is what James Bond should be. Not to mention how well written and portrayed every character is. Whether they're as brief as Cressida Bright or as extensive as Greenway and Moneypenny, and of course, Patrick Gibson's James Bond, everything feels valuable. Looking forward to making different choices and taking alternate routes that I didn't in my first playthrough, because this game encourages replayability, and so do I. My second 10/10 this year, and well deserved. I hope Hollywood sees what myself and many others do. Patrick Gibson is worthy of taking on the role of James Bond on the big screen.

items.quote:
Ogółem gra jest bardzo dobra, ale jest parę rzeczy, które są niedopracowane, lub dla mnie są minusami. 

Graficznie gra stoi na bardzo dobrym poziomie, ale na PS5 Pro niektóre tekstury to jest jakaś tragedia, istna pikseloza - niektóre elementy podłogi, albo zdjęcia, czy też napisy, itd. Jest to w sumie losowe, ale czytałem, że to faktycznie jest problem nie tylko na PS5.

Jeżeli chodzi o muzykę i audio jak dla mnie jest super i nie mam zastrzeżeń.

System walki wręcz mimo wszystko nie jest jakoś bardzo rozbudowany. Myślę, że mogli wykonać lepszą robotę, jeżeli chodzi o więcej kombinacji jeżeli chodzi o klawisze, bo aktualnie to jest kwestia wciskania dwóch guzików, lub spamowanie jednego. Wizualnie wygląda to dobrze, ale jeżeli chodzi o trudność, czy moje odczucia to mogłoby być lepiej. 

Bardzo drewniany model jazdy. Rozumiem, że nie na tym w tej grze się skupiamy i to tylko mały dodatek, ale mimo wszystko jest mega drewniany. Mało swobody ma gracz, jeżeli chodzi o prowadzenie pojazdu, responsywność jest słaba w kwestii gazu, czy skręcania w niektórych pojazdach.

Jeżeli chodzi o postęp w grze, to nie za bardzo podoba mi się fakt późnego dostania pistoletu z tłumikiem, bo jest to praktycznie w połowie gry. Preferowałbym go dostać od razu na początku i działać mega po cichu, ale niestety tak się nie da. Na początku również ograniczają zasób gadżetów, co rozumiem, ale preferowałbym możliwość wykorzystania wszystkich 4 gniazd do ich osadzenia. 

Samo strzelanie jest w porządku, ale dosyć bruździ tutaj fakt, że gdy jest ostra zadyma, to trzeba się skupiać na podnoszeniu broni i amunicji z przeciwników, bo ta bardzo szybko się kończy. Amunicja uzupełnia się dopiero, jak znajdziemy taką samą broń, a przeciwnicy walczą różną, wiec co chwila trzeba ją zmieniać.
Dosyć upierdliwe jest też ciągłe szukanie chemikaliów i urządzeń, aby ładować pasek gadżetów. W sensie rozumiem, że to jest mechanika gry, ale jest to dosyć monotonne i na pewno jakieś inne rozwiązanie mogłoby być lepsze. 

Przydałaby się jakaś osobna sala treningowa, aby mieć możliwość potrenowania sobie bez pośpiechu, bo fabuła ciągnie nas przez szkolenie, ale ono jest zbyt chaotyczne. W sensie nie ma możliwości powtórzenia na spokojnie tych rzeczy, tylko od razu przechodzisz z jednego mechanizmu na drugi. 

Symulacje taktyczne to jak dla mnie lekki nie wypał. W sensie nie za bardzo czuje chęć i potrzebę przechodzenia tego w ogóle. Nie wiem czego to kwestia, ale prawdopodobnie tego, że jest to bardzo powtarzalne, bo jak się przeszło już fabułę, to te lokacje się zna i to trochę zniechęca. Możliwe, że gdyby były one nowe, unikalne było by lepiej. Wprowadzenie losowości na pewno by urozmaiciło ten tryb.

Gra czasami jest zbyt łatwa. Nie ma tutaj za dużo takich przerywników w postaci, np. quick time eventów. Występują one praktycznie na samym końcu gry i polegają na wciśnięciu tego samego przycisku 3 razy. Dużo lepiej by tutaj sprawdziło się dodanie ich podczas wspinaczki, lub przemieszczania się w różnych lokacjach, lub też przy przesuwaniu rzeczy, itd. Tego mi brakowało, takiej większej ilości interakcji i wpływu na to co robimy.
Boli mnie trochę, że producenci nadal nie wykorzystują możliwości jakie daje Dual Sense, czy inne pady. Żyroskop, touchpad, mikrofon, itd. Użycie tych funkcji wzmocniło by znacznie odczucia z gry.

Krótki wątek z Bawmą. Po takim wprowadzeniu myślałem, że jednak będziemy mieć więcej do czynienia z nim. Rozczarowało mnie to, że po tym jak się wisiało nad krokodylami od razu był taki przeskok i praktycznie żadnej konwersacji z nim, ale wiemy, że będzie w DLC, więc mam nadzieję, że ten wątek zostanie nadrobiony.

Błędów jako tako za dużo nie doświadczyłem, ale czasami postać mimo wciskania klawiszu uniku i tak otrzymywała obrażenia. Było również pojedyncze zablokowanie się NPC na szafce.

Klimat bardzo mi się podobał. Bardzo piękne lokacje, różnorodne. Widać, że one żyją własnym życiem, są interakcje z NPCami i między nimi też dużo dialogów, które są ciekawe i przyjemnie się ich słucha.

Fabularnie nie mam się do czego przyczepić, szału nie było, ale tragedii też.

Pierwszoplanowe postacie odgrywały bardzo dobrze, przyjemnie się je oglądało i słuchało, mimika była w porządku. Miałem wątpliwości co do głównego bohatera, bo wiem, że przed premierą opinie były mieszane, ale dla mnie wybór tego aktora był jak najbardziej na plus. 

Ogólna moja ocena to 7/10 ale bardziej kierowałbym się na 7,5/10. Jest parę minusów i wad, ale w ogólnym rozrachunku bardzo przyjemnie spędziłem czas grając w tą produkcje.

items.quote: Bought this game because of all the hype and overwhelmingly positive reviews. Unfortunately, I regret it—honestly, I’m still frustrated with myself for falling for it.I expected something like a refined “Hitman” experience set in the Bond universe. That’s not what this is. Nothing here really stands out as better. The graphics are decent, but that’s about it. The story isn’t terrible, but it’s far from engaging. It follows a very typical Bond formula where the villain is always closer than you think, but it never manages to feel **** gameplay is extremely basic and, frankly, not enjoyable. You’re given almost no freedom in how to approach missions. Everything feels linear and restrictive. Even compared to Uncharted—which isn’t an open-world game—you feel significantly more freedom there than you do in First **** AI is disappointing, easily worse than what you’d find in most Hitman **** of the most frustrating aspects is the gadget system. The watch mechanics feel tedious, constantly forcing you to recharge it using random electronic objects scattered around. On top of that, collecting chemical products adds nothing meaningful to the experience. It feels like unnecessary filler.James Bond is supposed to have a license to kill, yet about 75% of the time you’re forced into hand-to-hand combat. It gets repetitive very quickly.I was already bored after 15 minutes, hoping it would improve—but it never did.After spending $100 CAD, I honestly feel misled. It makes me question how genuine those glowing reviews really were. Amazon has a lot of money, and it’s hard not to wonder.Verdict: Don’t buy it. You’ll likely get bored fast.
items.author: Phaasm

items.quote:
Not THAT good.

A mix of Hitman and Uncharted that only succeeds in wanting me to play those other games. The Hitman-esque open world sections are far too narrow and guided, completely losing the feeling of endless possibilities and replay-ability of the most recent trilogy. Uncharted style puzzle sections feel like a slog, not particularly challenging, and slow to get through simply because bond is locked at a snail’s walking pace. The hand to hand combat is fun, but once you get a gun, it’s too easy to simply headshot everyone, making you completely ditch the melee/gadgets. Even on Hard mode.

The resources system is painfully frustrating, and On multiple occasions, I found myself aimlessly walking around the map looking for chemical or electronic resources to get past a certain part, and at some points even restarting checkpoints to get my resources back because you absolutely need certain gadgets to get past certain parts. It all disincentivizes the use of gadgets in a very frustrating way. 

The story may very well be the saving grace of the whole thing. While not mind blowing, the core relationships are solid, and I found myself empathizing with a more characterized and fleshed out Bond than often appears in the films. However, I am extremely bored with the aesthetic of high tech capers like this. The magic and fun of bond are the cheesy gadgets, the over the top villains with often times ludicrous plans. With such a grounded story, I found the central plot to be very typical of any other espionage franchise following corruption and technology. It may be a contemporary take, but it doesn’t exactly feel as fun as the early films.

Uncharted 4 came out a decade ago. Same with the first Hitman remake. It’s remarkable to me that this game feels regressed from these by a fair amount. I feel the hype has a lot to do with the character and our hunger for simple, single player adventures like this. 

The basis is here, I just hope the team sees this first entry as a launchpad for sequels that can match or surpass the level of it’s inspirations, instead of feeling like a watered down mixture of them all.

items.author: gregor777

items.quote:
I think the most redeeming quality of this game is the overarching narrative. The wider plot contains thoughtful political intrigue, smokescreens, and espionage. Despite this, I think the writing falls short in the moment-to-moment aspects as it focuses on the more superficial connections and the sarcastic adolescent quips that are poorly delivered throughout. You know what they say about sarcasm, right? If you don't, then fear not, for you will certainly come to know by the end of the game, as every character has sarcasm woven into their DNA!Additionally, the narrative greatly struggles with pacing, with the initial third of the game moving too fast and final third being slow as molasses. This impacts character relationships, perceptions, and value. 

Gameplay is a major weak point for First Light. From melee combat, to gunfights, to driving, to stealthing, it is done at a sub-par level. The gameplay aspects have been executed in one of the most uninspired ways possible. I am sincerely disappointed because there is literally nothing that has been refined nor innovated upon. The enemy intelligence is lacklustre, the NPC behaviour is dumb as bricks, and the set pieces are dull imitations. 

-Melee combat may be crunchy, but it is underwhelming and bland. By the 2nd or 3rd mission, you will already have seen all melee combat animations/combos, stealth takedowns animations, and enemy types. By the 4th mission or so, you will have experienced the only unique fighting style and situation. Where is the refinement and/or innovation? They could have taken ideas from many different enemy types from the likes of Batman, God of War, Elden Ring, Spiderman, Dishonored, Uncharted, Mad Max, Assassins Creed, Yakuza, and I am sure a plethora of others. 

-The state of melee combat is compounded by a few things. As mentioned earlier, the FOV being far too close makes for a frustratingly claustrophobic experience. At times it can feel worse than Elden Ring, and even then, you can give that game a pass because you are slaying behemoths. 

-More often than not, fisticuffs take place in tight spaces with no lock on. No lock on is not that big of an issue, but it can get annoying if the camera is uncooperative.

-Immersion breaking ‘stealth’ takedowns. No choke holds or neck snapping. Straight up, judo tossing or smashing faces into inanimate objects before throat punching or face smashing. Crickets. 

-Reloading chemical weapons with hand sanitisers……would be funny in a Johnny English video game world. Not here though. 

-Guns lack oomph. Faster to dispatch enemies hand-to-hand. Aiming feels shoddy too. 

-Poorly implemented cover system. Splinter Cell: Blacklist, Uncharted, The Last of Us, all do it better.

-Clunky and erratic movement. Inconsistent jogging to sprinting, cover to cover does not feel smooth, Bond suddenly jumps up like a gazelle and sprints. Transitioning cover to cover in gunfights is also poorly implemented as you can be stuck in crouch mode. When sprinting during gunfights Bond’s agility skyrockets.

 -Forced walking sections with no auto walk or hold to walk. 



Decent graphics and wonderful use of lighting. Nothing outstanding here though. Optimisation is not up to scratch but that is an industry wide problem. Smoke grenades and driving fast really tanked my FPS and caused stutters. Poor audio design in my opinion too. During combat set pieces the music is over-powering and combined with explosions and such you can barely hear the dialogue. It really is a bit of a racket. There are also times during stealth or investigation where there is no music at all which feels off. 

A ridiculous amount of platforming that is nowhere near as exhilarating or visually impressive as other single player games like Tomb Raider and Uncharted. -Level design was talked about having multiple approaches, but these changes in approach are so small that it doesn’t feel like it at all. If you have experienced top notch level design from franchises like Deus Ex, MGS, Dishonored, Splinter Cell, and Prey then you will be thoroughly unimpressed here. 

-Bond is not charming at all. They keep saying he is, but the game suffers from not showing just telling. Nathan Drake would actually make a better Bond. -Greenway is a miserable git. Berates Bond whenever he can and shushes Bond for no reason during missions. Even after you find about his ordeal, you really do not warm up to him.

items.quote:
Классный боевик про молодого Бонда. Авторам удалось соблюсти баланс между нелинейностью хитмана и зрелищностью анчартед. Игра выглядит хорошо, может, не самый топ по графике, но современно и имеет хорошую оптимизацию. Плюс имеется хорошо проработанная физика объектов окружения, что на самом деле редкость в подобным играх.
Геймплейно она тяготеет к похождениям лысого убийцы, у нас есть обширные уровни с несколькими маршрутами, и мы вольны сами выбирать как проходить их - по стелсу, используя разнообразные гаджеты и предметы окружения, или в лобовую, отстреливаясь за укрытиями. Интеллект врагов неплохой, тела своих товарищей замечают издалека, стреляют довольно метко, покидывают гранаты, умеют обходить с флангов. Хотя часто не слышат шум буквально в паре метров от себя, но мб это уже условности. Прокачки нет вообще, что плюс, только гаджеты от Q и смекалка. Стрелять приятно, стрелять дают не всегда, поэтому Бонд умеет хорошо драться, к тому же владеет разными приёмчиками вроде подзывания врагов или их забалтывания. 
Сюжетно это какбы приквел ко всем фильмам серии, нам показывают становление Бонда как агента (еще без номера 007), как он вообще попал в МИ6, его первое знакомство с М и Q. Ну и отношения с женщинами, куда без них.
Как по мне, это лучшая игра во франшизе, в ней всё на своих местах.

items.quote:
Ce propose une aventure spectaculaire, portée par une excellente mise en scène et une ambiance digne des meilleurs films d'espionnage. L’histoire est prenante, avec plusieurs moments forts et une vraie dose d’émotion qui rendent le scénario agréable à suivre.
Les mécaniques de gameplay sont efficaces et les gunfights offrent de bonnes sensations. Les combats au corps-à-corps sont également une vraie réussite, avec des animations variées et des enchaînements dynamiques qui rendent chaque affrontement agréable. 
En revanche, les combats deviennent assez répétitifs au fil de l’aventure, et le manque de munitions oblige constamment à ramasser les armes des ennemis, ce qui casse souvent le rythme de l’action.
Le plus gros défaut reste l’absence de doublage français. Dans un jeu aussi dynamique, où l’attention est principalement portée sur le gameplay, il est difficile de lire les sous-titres en permanence. Les joueurs non bilingues risquent donc de passer à côté d’une grande partie de l’histoire, des dialogues et de certains éléments importants du scénario.
Enfin, un sprint un peu plus rapide aurait été apprécié, les déplacements entre les différents objectifs pouvant parfois sembler trop longs et casser le rythme de l’exploration. 
Malgré ces défauts, 007 First Light reste une très bonne expérience, grâce à son ambiance, sa mise en scène et son scénario captivant.

items.quote: What a ride, I’m so incredibly pleased with this game. It was a tall order for IOI to mix Uncharted & Hitman while simultaneously depicting a James Bond worthy of his name. But they really served that cocktail shaken, not stirred. It’s got witty writing, a perfect main actor, excellent pacing, frantic combat, skillful combat, and sneaky stealth. It’s very linear, which felt good and is necessary to achieve the excellent pacing. But the combat would occasionally confuse me whether it was okay to improvise, or absolutely not. Shorter loading times would’ve made this less problematic. The shooting was initially difficult for me, but once I improved my headshot skills it was a blast, it just wasn’t very clear that I really needed to master that technique at first. Wish the gauntlets would allow for more improvisation; flinging my gun into someone’s face, then rushing them hand to hand, stealing their gun and continuing the fight. Those were some of the best moments and I wanted more of it! The stealth bits worked great as a contrast to the action, and the bluff mechanic is a truly genius way to make Bond’s witty personality interactive! But I’m not a fan of stealth when it becomes a monotonous routine, and overusage of the Q-Watch was a problem for me. I struggle with Hitman’s general stealth mechanics too, and just like in Hitman I think it works best when it’s actually less systemic and more like a linear puzzle with a number of spectacular murder mystery solutions.Storywise, it does a good job even though I personally found it difficult to follow all the details. I got the broad strokes and was satisfied but perhaps not as entangled as **** technical aspects of the game are incredible on the audio visual side, outstanding work. But I had several crashes, a corrupted save file, the loading times really are jarringly long, and I’m missing a manual save system which I think is paramount in a stealth game. After finishing it I went back and played some of the best parts again, and doing that when I’d mastered the systems was an incredible experience. Would’ve been a 9/10 if that was my first run!

items.quote: 007 First Light is, above all, a James Bond film turned into a video game. It does not try to reinvent anything or revolutionize the genre, and in fact it borrows recognizable ideas from other action, stealth, and cinematic adventure titles. However, it combines them with such rhythm and precision that the result works wonderfully. It is one of those games that understands exactly what it wants to be: a direct, spectacular experience packed with moments designed to keep the player constantly engaged.Across its approximately 15-hour campaign, 007 First Light delivers a very well-paced experience, with a clearly cinematic structure and a constant succession of action scenes, infiltration sequences, and situations that feel unmistakably Bond. The sensation is that of being inside an interactive blockbuster, where every mission tries to offer something memorable and where there is rarely any room for boredom. Many of its mechanics may feel familiar from other video games, but what matters is that they are well integrated and always serve the **** of its greatest strengths lies in how it combines stealth with direct combat. The game allows many situations to be approached however the player prefers at any given moment, without making one option feel clearly wrong or giving the impression that you are playing “incorrectly”. You can move forward discreetly, use environmental resources, improvise, or resolve encounters in a more aggressive way, and in every case the experience flows naturally. That flexibility keeps the pace from ever slowing down and gives each section a constant sense of **** a technical level, 007 First Light also holds up very well. It is a visually polished game, with spectacular staging and a finish that does not fall behind current standards. Its presentation reinforces the feeling of playing through a modern spy film, with well-directed scenes, impactful action, and a rhythm that aims to deliver dopamine at every **** perhaps that is why it works so well: because it is the kind of game that feels increasingly rare nowadays. It does not invent new mechanics or reinvent the wheel, but it does aim for something we do not see often enough: being faithful to its license, being fun, and doing things right. It is the kind of single-player experience that is enjoyable from beginning to end and, precisely because it is so well paced, ends up feeling shorter than you would **** final impression is very positive. 007 First Light is not only an intense and highly entertaining cinematic adventure, but also a very promising starting point for a new line of 007 video games. Its formula has plenty of room to grow through future installments or DLCs, and it leaves the impression that, with this foundation, James Bond may finally have a modern video game series worthy of the character.

items.quote:
007 First Light is a stealth/action game.

You play as a young James Bond, the game starting out even before you become a 00 agent, on a mission where you end up attracting the attention of MI6 as a potential operative. You go through a training montage, training with other prospective 00 agents, and build some bonds with them, as well as your instructor, Greenway, who is a former 00 agent himself.

Of course, the game would not be a James Bond story if there weren’t twists and turns, and the game has a good number of plot twists. The obvious villain at the start of the game isn’t the main villain (though the actual main villain is not exactly subtle), and the game manages to take you through a variety of different locations and scenarios as you try and resolve the current crisis. It has a number of fun setpieces and you have to infiltrate a bunch of different places over the course of the story, with segments shifting between stealth, puzzle solving in more socially mingling environments, and gunplay segments where you have to blast your way through enemies and drive vehicles on chases.

The game thus alternates between these different modes to try and keep things fresh and varied, and while it works well from the perspective of mixing things up, unfortunately, it is also where the game falls down hardest.

The core of the problem is that none of these segments are particularly good – the driving is lackluster, the social mingling is decent but ends up being a bit samey over time, the stealth mechanics are pretty much the same throughout the game (use something to distract the person -> sneak past them), and the gunplay is pretty basic and repetitive, without much variety in enemies. There are a few things that mix up the gameplay a bit more, but all in all, the gameplay is really the weakest part of this game – it ends up feeling repetitive by the end of it because there just isn’t enough depth to any of the game’s mechanics.Story-wise, the story is solid enough, with fun, well-acted characters (both friend and foe) and an overall solid enough plot. James Bond is likeable, and is a bit impetuous and independent here, showing a stubborn streak. He works well enough, and the implication that there were other 00s before him (along with various easter egg references to movies/stories) is fun. Moneypenny, Q, M, Greenway, your fellow 00 recruits, and some other friends and foes are fun enough characters, and work pretty well all told.

Overall, I think this game is pretty decent, and I feel like this game does a much better job of “making you feel like James Bond” than any other 007 game ever has; this game has a lot more actual spying going on, with you engaging in social interactions and “hiding in plain sight” rather than having to sneak through every area behind waist-high walls or just blast your way through everything.

But I think the game mechanics’ shallowness holds the game back from absolute greatness.

items.quote:
First of all, let me just say that 007: First Light is a GOOD game. I enjoyed playing it and I want to be clear on that. BUT if I’m being honest it comes up just a little bit short of my expectations. Specifically the hand to hand combat is really quite basic and can be kinda janky/clunky feeling. It’s not bad, I’m not saying that at all. But for as amazing as this game LOOKS, the melee combat could (and should) be better and more in depth and it could play smoother at times. I think it could benefit from having a dedicated button like Left trigger/bumper or maybe just a simple target lock…SOMETHING that can square bond up to his enemy when fighting hand to hand. The environment is fairly interactive during combat which is good but they don’t get very creative with it, I mean, ok you can throw a guy against/into the all the stuff but typically it doesn’t result in anything that’s particularly unique or especially interesting. Idk, I’m just saying that using the surrounding environment in melee combat isn’t as awesome as it could be. But I digress, this is a minor critique. Also, I’m not saying they should’ve just copied another game but it would benefit from having more of a free-flow type of combat system like the Rocksteady Arkham games or Sleeping Dogs if you remember that game…and like I said, smoother…like more fluid looking/feeling. 

Let me remind you once again tho…its not bad by any means, the melee combat, it’s just kinda clunky and plain. I say this as a long time fan of  Hitman so I have high standards for IO’s finished product because I know how talented they are.

Also, the stealth…it’s fine. It’s ok. It could also be improved upon. I like how you use the Bond gadgets to assist with stealth but the environment is really only set up for turning things off/on so idk what but I feel like there could be more variety in that regard. Just my own personal opinion, maybe I’m alone in thinking that. 

But Ok, that’s pretty much it. Those things are really my only critiques. All in all It’s still a damn good time. It’s basically like a Bond themed Uncharted game…which is exactly what I want out of a James Bond game. Most of all, I’m really REALLY glad that they didn’t neuter the James Bond character. You know…“for the modern audience” as developers like to say…right before they are about to ruin a game out of fear of offending literally anyone. But I’m happy to report they DIDN’T! They did a great job on that front. He’s James frickin Bond alright. He’s smooth, he’s suave, he blows **** up, he drives kickass cars, he fights bad guys on top of runaway trains n **** reckless, he’s got balls the size of watermelons and he bangs beautiful women all over the planet and we love him for it, dammit! 

I officially declare that 007: First Light is a good game. It’s not great…but so what? Bottom line is that it’s a return to form for this game franchise and I for one am glad Bond is back. Really looking forward to the next installment as I expect it will surely be even bigger, better and Bondier

I score it 8 Walther PPK’s out of 10 .
