items.quote: 007 First Light is exactly the kind of game James Bond fans have been waiting for. Rather than simply recreating the formula established by decades of films, it successfully tells an origin story that feels fresh while remaining unmistakably Bond. It balances espionage, action, intrigue, and cinematic spectacle with remarkable confidence, creating an experience that is as enjoyable to play as it is to **** of the game's greatest achievements is its narrative. The story unfolds like a high-quality spy thriller, full of twists, memorable set pieces, and believable character development. Watching Bond evolve from a talented but inexperienced agent into the iconic secret operative we know adds genuine emotional weight to the adventure. It captures the essence of Ian Fleming's character while giving players something entirely new.Visually, the game is stunning. Every location is beautifully realized, from luxurious casinos and bustling cities to remote facilities and breathtaking landscapes. The level of detail is exceptional, making each environment feel authentic and alive. Combined with impressive lighting, facial animation, and cinematic camera work, the presentation consistently feels worthy of a blockbuster **** performances deserve enormous praise. Every major character delivers convincing and nuanced acting, helping the story maintain its momentum from beginning to end. The voice cast brings personality and credibility to every conversation, while the motion capture elevates emotional scenes far beyond what is typically expected in action games. It's one of those rare titles where dialogue feels just as engaging as the gameplay itself.Gameplay strikes an excellent balance between stealth, investigation, gadgets, gunplay, and high-octane action. Rather than forcing players into constant firefights, First Light embraces the fantasy of being a secret agent. There are multiple ways to approach objectives, rewarding careful planning as much as quick thinking. Whether infiltrating enemy compounds, gathering intelligence, or improvising during missions that inevitably spiral out of control, the game constantly makes you feel like **** pacing is another highlight. Quiet investigative moments transition naturally into explosive action sequences without ever feeling forced. Every mission introduces new mechanics, locations, or scenarios that keep the experience engaging throughout the campaign. It understands that variety is essential for a spy adventure, and it delivers that variety **** soundtrack perfectly complements the atmosphere, blending orchestral tension with classic Bond-inspired themes. Combined with excellent sound design, it creates an immersive experience that constantly reinforces the feeling of starring in your own 007 movie.Perhaps what impressed me most is how confidently the developers established their own interpretation of James Bond. Instead of relying purely on nostalgia or imitating the films scene for scene, they crafted an identity that respects the franchise while giving it room to evolve. It feels modern without losing the sophistication, charm, and elegance that define **** only reason I didn't award it a perfect score has nothing to do with the game's quality. Simply put, spy-action adventures are not my favorite genre. If they were, I could easily see this being one of my favorite games of the year. Judging it purely on its own merits, it's an exceptionally polished, cinematic, and thoroughly entertaining experience.007 First Light proves that James Bond belongs in modern gaming just as much as he belongs on the big screen. It's stylish, intelligent, beautifully crafted, and consistently fun from beginning to **** outstanding spy thriller and one of the best adaptations the franchise has ever received.8/10

One of the best gaming experiences I have had in a while. It plays like a mixture of the best elements from Hitman, Uncharted and the Arkham Series.
I was somewhat worried that the game would demand strict adherence to stealth principles, including auto-fail when spotted. The balance on this front is very good as the game incentivizes stealth but can be completed without it. This allows for a greater choice surrounding how to solve challenges, reduces frustration compared to auto-failing, and presents some very tense situations where you can be quickly overwhelmed in combat.

My only real negative is that the poor decision making of AI can break immersion sometimes. While it makes sense to code in some opportunity for the player to control engagement, sometimes nearby enemies can be laughably oblivious.

I highly recommend giving this a go.
items.author: Hotburger420

items.quote: I really, really enjoyed 007 First Light. What impressed me most was the way the missions are designed and how seamlessly they integrate story and character development into the gameplay. I was genuinely surprised by how much I liked the characters and how attached I became to them over the course of the game. The story remained engaging and exciting from beginning to end.  Most importantly, the game absolutely captures the feeling of the best Bond films. Any concerns that the game might prioritize messaging over storytelling proved completely unfounded. At its core, this is a thrilling James Bond adventure. The mix of exploring sandbox-style levels, gathering intelligence, stealth gameplay, and transitioning into intense hand-to-hand combat and gunfights worked wonderfully for me.  I only have two major criticisms that keep this from being a perfect 10/10.  First, I experienced multiple crashes on my PS5 Pro, particularly during loading screens. While the game generally ran well, having to quit and restart several times was frustrating and occasionally broke the immersion.  Second, I'm increasingly bothered by the amount of handholding in modern games, and 007 First Light is no exception. Why does every climbable surface need to be marked with yellow paint? It feels like lazy game design. The constant button prompts are equally unnecessary. After vaulting over obstacles hundreds of times, I don't need another reminder telling me to "Press X to vault." Developers should trust players more and assume they can remember basic controls after the tutorial.  Those issues aside, 007 First Light was an incredibly fun experience. And that's exactly what I want from a 15–20 hour story-driven game. It's the kind of game I'll happily revisit every few years, and that's probably the highest compliment I can give it.

items.quote: James Bond First Light plays it very safe gameplay wise. It feels like a hybrid between Uncharted and the Hitman series. The stealth and parkor mechanics lack depth. The story is very Bond, leaning heavily on stereotypical plot devices from the films. The gadgets and guns lack variety. That said the way the environment reacts to your character during fighting sequences allowing you to improvise multiple ways to kill bad guys is a real step forward, I hope this is used in future story games. I like the spying, hacking, eves dropping to get the necessary intel to progress the game. But beyond that the puzzle solving is pretty simple. It would be cool if future titles like this were more open allowing Bond to infiltrate places with different methods either by stealth, spy craft or more varied parkor elements such as grappling hooks and zip lines etc. It was quite difficult to feel much sympathy for any of the characters unlike titles like The Last Of Us. A bit more human emotion rather than detached soundbites would make the game feel more grounded. They did it with the Daniel Craig films but missed the mark slightly here. The vehicle elements were really enjoyable although more car chases with higher stakes would have been good. In conclusion, the game has some good elements that I enjoyed but there was just a little bit missing to me it a true classic that I would like to come back to once I finished the story. But this is has great potential for future sequels.

items.quote:
Let’s be entirely honest: if you strip away the 007 logo, the licensed music, and the Walther PPK, 007 First Light is a remarkably mediocre, generic action game.I’m genuinely baffled by the glowing praise this game is receiving. It seems like a massive case of "franchise starvation"—we haven't had a major Bond game in over a decade, and everyone is so desperate for one that the bar has dropped through the floor. Add in the immense goodwill critics have for IO Interactive after the Hitman trilogy, and it feels like people are reviewing the studio’s reputation rather than the actual game on the **** you went into this expecting the brilliant, open-ended sandbox freedom that IO is famous for, you are going to be severely disappointed. Here is why the "masterpiece" narrative doesn't hold up under actual scrutiny:

1. Heavily Scripted, "On-Rails" Boredom - The game sacrifices mechanical depth for cinematic choreography. It is aggressively linear and filled with restrictive scripting. When a spy game forces you through rigid Quick-Time Events (QTEs) just to handle basic narrative moments, it ceases to be an engaging stealth experience and becomes a playable movie.

2. Zero Stakes or Real Challenge - A great espionage game relies on tension. You should feel like an elite agent operating on a razor's edge. Instead, Bond can essentially stroll through high-security facilities with virtually no friction or threat. The AI is flat, the action feels entirely unrealistic, and the pacing is completely halted by clunky mechanics—like a combat system that forces you to wait for enemies to show "intent" before you can react naturally.

3. A Sci-Fi Identity Crisis - Bond works best when it's grounded in high-stakes, classic espionage. First Light veers way too far into generic tech-thriller/sci-fi territory with its focus on the THEIA supercomputer. It feels less like Ian Fleming or Casino Royale and more like a futuristic sci-fi shooter that lost its identity.

4. Check-The-Box Branding - The classic Bond staples are entirely skin-deep here. The Q-Lab feels uninspired and lame, giving you glorified keys for specific doors rather than clever gadgets that alter how you play. Worse, the "love interests" are completely hollow, dropped into the narrative without an ounce of chemistry just to tick a box on a developer checklist that says: "Look, it’s a Bond game!"

Final Verdict007 - First Light isn't a broken, buggy disaster, which is why it's getting safe, lazy passes from supporters. But being polished and shiny doesn't make it good. It is a shallow, rushed, on-rails experience that trades rewarding gameplay for cinematic window dressing. It’s an okay generic action game, but it is a terrible Bond game. Don't let the hype train fool you.

items.quote:
The game is "pretty good." My score is entirely for gameplay, but the visuals, voice acting, story, and so on, are all good to great. Bond's VA especially. 

But the gameplay...

1. Definitely nails the spy/espionage feel with the gadget mechanic. Gadgets involve resource management, which is great for combat but can be an unnecessary hinder to the spy puzzle solving when you've got to run around looking for charge/chemicals. A minor nuisance, but when the game gives you recharging resources it makes me think, "This would feel so much better as the norm..."

2. Combat is lacking though. In melee, parries are not satisfying or worth it because you only get the counter on the last hit, unless the enemy finishes with a grab in which case you cannot parry at all. Therefore.. just dodge all attacks/grabs and punish with your combos. The game gives you lots of options, but when dash attack, punch, gut punch, grab+slam either finishes or grants a takedown opportunity, it becomes repetitive.

3. Personally don't care much for the range of guns but the game not only gives you bullet time but also aim assist (even on "hard"). Not only that, you can just run around and enemies have very poor accuracy. I get that Bond films are full of action but some moments feel like a generic shooter game on easy.

Ultimately I had a good experience (despite it being quite buggy, experiencing a soft lock, crashes, and minor bugs but I'm forgiving a new release from a smaller developer) and would be open to the next Bond game hoping they make improvements. It was rather short though, about 15 hours.

items.quote: First Light is a great introduction to what could become the next generation of James Bond games. It strikes a solid balance between espionage, action, stealth, hacking, and combat, keeping things fresh enough that the gameplay rarely feels repetitive. The story is engaging and does its job well, even if it’s not particularly memorable once the credits roll. One of the game’s strongest aspects is its progression system. The more you play, the more capable both you and Bond become. There’s a satisfying learning curve as you gradually master hand-to-hand combat, close- and long-range gunplay, stealth, and hacking. By the end, you genuinely feel like a skilled 00 agent who knows exactly what he’s doing. My biggest criticism is the level design. While the mission-based sandbox stealth/action game approach offers plenty of freedom within each mission, I often found myself wishing the game felt a little more open. Some environments can feel surprisingly restrictive and even a bit claustrophobic at times. Expanding the scale and giving players more room to approach objectives creatively would be a great step forward for future entries. That said, this is an incredibly promising start for IO Interactive’s new Bond franchise. Here’s hoping they get to keep their license to kill and continue building on this foundation in the next game.

items.quote: 007 First Light ReviewIntroductionJames Bond is a name that many gamers haven't heard in quite some time. In fact, it's been nearly 14 years since the last major James Bond game release in 2012. For those of us who grew up during the Nintendo 64 and PlayStation era, that's hard to believe. There was a time when it felt like a new Bond game arrived almost every ****, IO Interactive, the studio best known for the Hitman franchise, has accepted the mission of bringing the world's most famous secret agent back to gaming. But does 007 First Light successfully capture the magic of classic Bond games, or does it fall short of its target?Let's find out.StoryIn 007 First Light, players step into the shoes of a young James Bond before he becomes the legendary agent known as 007. Bond begins his journey serving in the Royal Navy, but during a mission, disaster strikes when his helicopter is shot down. As the sole survivor, Bond must fight his way through hostile territory and find a path to safety.While navigating the enemy camp, Bond receives assistance from Moneypenny, who guides him through the extraction process. Following his rescue, he is recruited into MI6's newly re-established Double-0 Program, beginning his transformation from an inexperienced soldier into one of the world's most skilled spies.Training plays a significant role in the early portion of the game, introducing players to Bond's future colleagues and mentor, Greenway. The training sequences feel like something straight out of an action movie, complete with montage moments reminiscent of classic films such as Rocky. It's entertaining, well-paced, and does an excellent job of establishing Bond's **** of the standout training missions places Bond in a nightclub where he must identify and make contact with a target among a crowd of agents. It's here that the game truly begins to embrace the spy fantasy, allowing players to utilize gadgets, deception, and intelligence gathering.However, once Bond enters the field on his first official assignment, things quickly spiral out of control. What begins as a routine operation evolves into a much larger conspiracy, forcing Bond to uncover dangerous secrets and prove that reviving the Double-0 Program was the right **** story delivers plenty of twists, memorable characters, and exciting set pieces while providing a compelling origin story for one of fiction's most iconic agents.GameplayTo make things easier, I'll break gameplay into five categories:•	Shooting•	Navigation and Stealth•	Gadgets•	Close-Quarters Combat•	DrivingShootingPrior to release, I had heard mixed opinions regarding the game's shooting mechanics. Some early impressions described them as merely average. After experiencing them myself, I completely disagree.Unlike action-heavy franchises such as Uncharted, Gears of War, or even some previous Bond games, 007 First Light does not rely on constant gunfights. Instead, combat encounters occur at specific moments and trigger what the game calls "License to Kill" sequences.During these encounters, Bond moves in and out of cover while engaging enemies in cinematic firefights. Environmental destruction plays a major role, allowing players to shoot explosive barrels, gas tanks, and pipelines. By activating Bond's Q Watch, players can identify environmental hazards and opportunities.Several combat abilities add depth to firefights. Bullet Time returns, slowing down time and allowing players to line up precise shots. Shooting enemies in the hands can disarm them, while leg shots cause them to stumble, creating opportunities for melee takedowns.Ammunition is intentionally limited, encouraging creativity. One of my favorite mechanics is being able to throw an empty weapon at an enemy, stunning them long enough to close the distance and finish them with a melee **** shooting may not be constant, but when it happens, it's exciting, satisfying, and highly cinematic.Navigation and Stealth007 First Light is a third-person action-adventure game, meaning players will spend a significant amount of time climbing, traversing environments, and exploring mission areas.Bond's movement feels very similar to Nathan Drake from the Uncharted series, and honestly, that's not a bad thing. Movement is smooth, responsive, and enjoyable throughout the **** game also provides multiple ways to approach objectives. If players prefer a more direct approach, they can use Instinct Points to bluff their way past guards by posing as authorized personnel. Instinct Points are earned through stealth actions, intelligence gathering, and eavesdropping on conversations.Alternatively, players can lure enemies away from patrol routes, perform stealth takedowns, or create distractions using objects such as radios and vacuum **** variety of options allows missions to feel flexible and rewards players for approaching situations creatively.GadgetsThis is where 007 First Light truly shines.

Baştan sona kadar beni kendine bağlamayı başaran bir oyun oldu. Atmosferi, sinematik anlatımı, oynanış çeşitliliği, görevlere farklı yöntemlerle yaklaşabilme özgürlüğü, duygusal anları ve gizem unsurlarıyla neredeyse her yönüyle çok başarılı buldum. Oyun boyunca sürekli yeni şeyler görüp deneyimleyebiliyorsunuz ve bu da temponun hiç düşmemesini sağlıyor.

(Mini Spoiler)
Olumsuz olarak değerlendirebileceğim tek kısım, yanlış hatırlamıyorsam Chapter 7’de yer alan Webb Industries bölümüydü. Bu görev bana gereğinden fazla uzun geldi ve büyük ölçüde bulmaca çözmeye odaklandığı için zaman zaman temposunu kaybetti. Ancak görevin final kısmını bunun dışında tutuyorum; çünkü son bölümleri oldukça etkileyiciydi. Bunun haricinde oyundaki her bölüm ve her mekan büyük bir özenle tasarlanmış. Gerek görsel tasarım gerekse atmosfer açısından ziyaret ettiğimiz her yer kendine özgü bir kimliğe sahip.

Oyunun uzunluğu da beni şaşırtan konulardan biri oldu. Açıkçası daha kısa süreceğini düşünüyordum ancak beklediğimden daha uzun bir deneyim sundu ve bu konuda da beklentilerimi fazlasıyla karşıladı. İçerik miktarı, hikaye akışı ve görev çeşitliliği sayesinde hiçbir zaman aceleye getirilmiş hissi vermedi.

Genel olarak değerlendirdiğimde, 007 First Light bu yıl şu ana kadar oynadığım en iyi oyun oldu. Sunduğu deneyim, atmosfer ve hikaye anlatımı sayesinde benim için unutulmaz yapımlar arasına girmeyi başardı. items.quote:
It’s a mystery to me why this game is so popular. From a game design perspective, I think it gets almost everything wrong. It plays like a game from more than ten years ago—yet it’s an inferior version of Uncharted 4, Hitman trilogy, Last of us or Detroit Become Human. 

All the driving sequences are completely superfluous and could easily have been cutscenes. They offer absolutely no added value to the gameplay. 

But the gameplay issues already start with the fact I can only throw objects directly at enemies. Why can’t I throw them elsewhere—like in real life, or to distract enemies the way you do in the much better Hitman Trilogy? Even without comparing it to Hitman, aren't I supposed to be a spy—or at least a human—who can throw objects anywhere to distract someone? Way less options than in other games and invisible walls everywhere—this game is very restrictive.

Generally, the whole game feels "on rails," as if I’m not even really playing it myself. There are zero stakes; most of the time, I just don't care—you simply blast your way through. The tools are way to easy to use you stop in front of some guy and shoot it at them unnoticed.

The thing is in a hitman game I feel like I wanna figure out one of the many options to solve the mission, I feel excited, there are stakes, there is thrill. In this game it takes you so much by the hand you dont even feel like you are playing it which results in you not being invested at all. I had to force myself to finish the game, and the longer I played, the more the missions felt like filler to stretch the playthough time.

The only good thing about it is the training montage right at the start, that’s a cool idea how it blends from one thing to another. It’s kind of funny, really: experienced players eventually get bored of games where you just shoot and beat up everything in sight via wild button-mashing, so they discover masterpieces like the Hitman trilogy—a relatively realistic agent simulation. Then First Light comes along and plays like a game for five-year-olds. Is this the level where we at now? Wild button mashing from 2010 is goty apparently smh

items.quote: This is the first James Bond video game in 14 years. It's also the best one since the N64 classic "Goldeneye". The plot is so good that it could've been used for the next 007 movie. And actor Patrick Gibson absolutely nails the cocky swagger that the iconic British spy is known for. The campaign lasts about 15 hours, but the replay value comes from numerous choices you can make to move the story forward. In addition, there are also "Tactical Simulation" challenge maps. With "Escalations", the goal is to simply dispatch every enemy. In "Operations", you complete objectives while avoiding or stealth killing enemies. Fans of "Splinter Cell" or Bond games such as "Everything or Nothing" and "Bloodstone" will love the ride. Overall, I'd rate this with a 9 out of 10.

007 First Light is, without a doubt, the best James Bond game ever made. Simple as that.

IO Interactive absolutely nailed every single detail. The game is packed with references to both the movies and the books—everything from items scattered across the map to the characters, and even the way Bond behaves.
The exploration, gameplay, and both the gunplay and hand-to-hand combat feel **** be honest,

I wasn't hyping this game up at all before launch. But I was so impressed by what I saw that I bought it the second reviews rolled in from people I actually trust. The game is incredibly faithful to the character and Ian Fleming's vision—and I say this as someone who has read several of the books and watched all the movies multiple times. Sure, the story is a modern-day reimagining of Bond's origin and takes some creative liberties, but everything was handled with so much respect and with ZERO woke stuff.

It’s not flawless; while playing, I can occasionally spot a few missed opportunities and minor rough edges. But those are just nitpicks. As a whole, the game is exceptional and absolutely deserves a sequel. I just hope they maintain the same level of respect in the next one and keep the same dev team on board.

Bottom line: if you love 007, you need to play this game.

items.quote:
I think this game will polarize…
007 First Light is a breath of fresh air and one of the most enjoyable action-adventure games I’ve played in a while. 
The visuals are absolutely stunning, the Bond atmosphere is spot on and the game perfectly captures the charm, wit, and style you’d expect from 007. The combat feels impactful and exciting, and the variety of missions keeps things fresh throughout the adventure.

My biggest criticism is that the game can be a little too restrictive at times. Objectives are often marked immediately, leaving little room for exploration or figuring things out on your own. I was hoping for something a bit closer to Hitman, where you’re encouraged to investigate and experiment more. Some sections also feel extremely linear, and a frustrating boss encounter in the middle of the game briefly brought the experience to a halt by forcing a very specific approach instead of letting the player tackle it more freely.

That said, none of these issues were enough to seriously hurt my enjoyment. The game quickly regained its momentum afterwards, and the highs are simply too good to ignore. From start to finish, I had a great time. It’s stylish, varied, genuinely feels like James Bond and by the end I was already excited for a sequel. 

If I had one wish for the sequel, it would be for the devs to trust the player’s intelligence and creativity a little more. Give us more room to explore, investigate and approach objectives in our own way instead of immediately pointing us toward the solution. The foundations are already excellent, and a little more freedom could make the next game truly special, or in other words, a 10 out of 10.

Score: 8/10

items.quote:
I think it's a beautiful game.

Beautifully written, acted.

Beautiful gameplay, beautiful graphics, sound design.

I was quite cynical about the game when it got announced because I wondered how IOI would capture the essence of this character, but to my surprise they have done so perfectly.

The game has an awesome cast of characters, all of them serving different purposes to the main story, al well layered beyond the usual, this character betrayed you, this one didn't, type of twists and usual turns.

The gameplay is like a bit more powerful and melee focused Hitman, with gadgets that allow you to alter stuff around your environment and stun enemies. The focus very much isn't in just attacking enemies or shooting at them though; there's those moments, and those moments are handled well, but generally, this is a game that threads between all the things Bond does in films.

You're infiltrating, fighting, shooting, platforming, charming, all the while you're investigating and completing missions.

I was also concerned about the inclusion of some celebrities and influencers, but generally this is handled well and it comes off more charmingly & silly, rather than exploitative or tacky.

What I would criticize though is the focus at times. Like there's a wonderful mission where you're infiltrating with a partner into a building. At multiple points you're left to wonder how to open a locked door or reached a ledge. I would figure this stuff out but the game wouldn't let me actually interact or complete my goals until a set amount of time had passed and my partner mentioned the solution to me.

I remember God of War: Ragnarok being heavily criticized for spoiling the solutions to puzzles before you could figure them out. This does something similar, but in my opinion, more annoying; it waits till the NPC's spoil the solution in order to let you continue playing the game. It got quite annoying in that mission in particular, but thankfully it wasn't something that came up that much afterwards.

I also think the pacing can be a bit slow at the start and I don't like the - once again - arbitrary always online implementation for Tacsim mode. This is a mode you get after playing a while in the main story that lets you experiment with an escalation system similar to Hitman games throughout different missions in the campaign, the problem is that it is always online for... reasons... leaderboards? Maybe? I don't know... it has a challenge system and unlocks for suits if you're to complete each challenge of each mission, however, the unlocks INCLUDING THE PRE-ORDER COSTUMES can only be used in Tacsim mode........

These are the issues I've encountered with the game, but generally, speaking purely about the campaign. I think it's a memorable and beautifully crafted experience. It can be slow at times and it can be quite guided at times, and this last issue conflicts with the game's own incentive to try and play it your own way. But even then, it's a remarkable experience, despite these issues, the acting, writing, and the awesome set pieces and gameplay sequences, work for the most part in creating something truly special.

items.quote: 007 First Light isn't a perfect game. The enemy AI is weak, technical issues prevent a flawless overall impression, and the gunfights don't quite reach the level of the excellent stealth mechanics. Nevertheless, IO Interactive has achieved something remarkable. The studio understands the DNA of James Bond better than many film adaptations of recent years. The gripping origin story, the flexible mission design, and the excellent espionage sequences truly make you feel like a budding 00 agent. Anyone who enjoys intelligent stealth games, thrilling spy stories, and classic Bond flair will find one of the most interesting action-adventure games of the year here. Not everything is perfect, but the direction is right – and it leaves you eager for more missions from this young James Bond.

A MUST BUY for any gamer, not only Bond fans

007 First Light is an incredible Bond experience and, for me, a perfect game. I played it on PlayStation 5, and what impressed me most is how complete it feels: a long, cinematic adventure that plays like several great Bond movies in one.

 The lack of noticeable loading screens, the smooth transitions, the beautiful locations, and the strong performance make it feel like one continuous movie. 
The missions are varied, the gameplay allows room for combat, stealth, gadgets, and creativity, and every mission has its own memorable identity.
The visuals, music, art direction, and Lana Del Rey theme are all excellent.
 This is a love letter to James Bond fans, but also a must-play for anyone who enjoys cinematic action games, adventure shooters, stealth, or story-driven experiences.

007 First Light is not just a great Bond game. It is a game every player should experience.

items.quote:
007 feels a lot like “0047 First Light,” and that works in its favor. The sandbox design, social stealth, and creative assassinations will feel familiar to Hitman fans, with added cinematic flair and Bond gadgets.

When it clicks, it is genuinely fun. Sneaking through crowded spaces, navigating levels, and pulling off clean takedowns all feel satisfying. The visuals, music, and pacing do a lot to sell the fantasy of being a junior spy.

It is not consistent. Combat and gadgets feel clunky at first and take time to settle. Some sections drag, with too much time spent slowly searching for ledges, crawlspaces, keycards, or hidden panels. The launch issues did not help either. Crashes and lost progress forced me to replay hours, and even though stability improved, that stuck with me.

The real problem is the product placement. It is constant and impossible to ignore. Bond is always tied to specific brands, from his watch to his cars to the environments around him. It stops feeling like part of the world and starts feeling like advertising. Paying $70 while being pushed ads aggressively breaks immersion and leaves a bad taste. 

The core gameplay is strong, but this is where I draw the line. Because of the product placement, this is a not recommended, and I will ramp up my efforts to be aware of product placement in games before purchasing in the future.

items.quote:
It’s a game that doesn’t take risks; it plays it safe, and if you’ve played Hitman before, this is basically it. Nothing revolutionary here, and it doesn't feel fresh at all.    

Setting & Exploration: The atmosphere is great, and the levels are highly detailed and fun to explore. However, there were only a few missions where I actually enjoyed this.    

Combat & AI: The combat is pretty shallow, and the gunplay is very simple and easy. The AI is dumb as a brick; at no point did I think, "Holy sht, that was clever, I didn't even see that guy flanking me."* It’s incredibly easy to stay alive in this game.    

Story: For those who enjoy 007 movies, the story is really cool. It's a bit predictable, but it felt like watching a new James Bond movie.    

Pacing: To artificially extend the game's length, they throw a bunch of filler BS in the middle just to waste your time. They could have given the player more freedom.    

Gameplay Formula: The approach to solving challenges follows the exact same formula the entire game: you get close to people talking, press Y, and listen to them say something so you can get a clue and progress. This holds the player's hand way too much; it could have been less guided. Other than that, you just scout the people around you, grab a keycard, and move on to the next section.    

Replay Value: Replay value is non-existent. Once you beat the game, you’ve seen it all. It made me wish there were multiple story paths depending on how you complete a mission. That would actually make me want to replay it to see the rest. Heck, maybe even new levels that you couldn't access in a single playthrough. (Like The Witcher 2, where if you side with the elf, you go to one area, and if you side with the human, you go to another—and there's no way to explore both in one run).

Summary: If you’re a 007 fan, go for it. If you’re not that into it, the best part—which is the story—won't make much of a difference to you.

This game was a huge letdown for me, personally. It has some redeeming aspects; a unique AI story, fun combat, occasionally great dialogue, and eye candy graphics. But it feels like there was an equal amount of moments that utterly broke my suspension of disbelief, a lot of hand wavy/tropey plot devices that feel better suited for an 80s b-list film, painfully linear and repetitive gameplay with few ways to approach an objective, and some nauseatingly bad dialogue. It flip flops between these two extremes quite often. Repeatedly I found myself wondering “how is this game getting mostly positive reviews?” 

Also, it was surprisingly buggy for me on the base PS5. Tons of controller issues, janky combat, character stuck on terrain, one hard crash, and some terrible stuttering at later sections of the game.

Perhaps I hyped myself up too much, but in the end I found myself rushing to finish it just to get it over with, sell my copy, and play something else. I have no desire to replay it. Maybe IO can polish over those rough areas for the sequels, we’ll see. 

For now this is a 6/10 at best for me, maybe a 7/10 if I’ve had some coffee.

items.quote:
Disappointing considering what IOI are capable of producing. 

I appreciate this is not a Hitman game, but they could have taken more from that series and applied it here. 

For example, in Hitman you have a location and within that are all the resources and intelligence available to complete your objective; then it's up to you to figure it out. 

First Light, however, is so on-rails you never really feel like you're in control. There was one segment I recall where guards denied entry to an area - but the camera immediately pans to an air vent that the player character happens to be standing right next to. You're not really given the chance to work stuff out for yourself. 

The driving sections are largely pointless as there's nowhere to go other than where the game is pointing you - they may as well be cut-scenes with no player interaction. 

There are other annoying elements, too - guards will have infinite ammo but drop weapons with 2 rounds in them. Combat could do with a camera lock or enemy focus option, as sometimes Bond will end up facing away from combat altogether. 

There are positives - the story is solid and very on-brand, the characters are well done, the environments look great, and the sound design is very good too. I loved the movie-montage style training that forms the tutorial. 

It's sadly just very boring to play - I find myself wishing that they'd just re-skinned Hitman and placed that game into these locations.

items.quote:
A Masterclass in Action-Espionage: 

007 First Light is an absolute triumph and easily one of the most incredible gaming experiences I’ve had in years. IO Interactive hasn’t just made a great Bond origin story, they’ve set a new high bar for the action-adventure genre. Playing this on a PS5 Pro paired with a 65" LG C4 OLED takes the presentation to an entirely different level.

The Good:

• Phenomenal Story & Pacing: The narrative is gripping from start to finish. It anchors you perfectly into this younger, building version of Bond, making you feel the weight of his journey to earn that double-0 status.

• Industry-Leading Combat: The combat is arguably the best I’ve ever played in a third-person game. It is fluid, aggressive, and highly improvisational, even outpacing heavyweights like Assassin’s Creed that are entirely built around physical engagement. The environmental takedowns and parry mechanics make every single brawl feel incredibly rewarding.

• Incredible Attention to Movement Detail: One of my favorite details is the sheer fluidity and accuracy of the character movement. When Bond walks up or down stairs, or navigates uphill and downhill terrain, his feet and body adjust perfectly to the slope. A lot of modern AAA games skimp out on this kind of animation detail, but here, it adds an immense layer of grounded realism to the exploration. 

• High-End Character Visuals & Display Performance: By and large, the graphics are stellar. The facial animations capture a fantastic level of nuance and emotion, and the hair textures are remarkably detailed. On the LG C4 OLED, the contrast and ink-black levels make the dark, stealth-heavy environments look stunning, while the PS5 Pro keeps the overall image incredibly sharp and responsive.

The Flaws: 

• Inconsistent Texture Polish: While the major visual presentation is gorgeous, there is a noticeable lack of polish on certain environmental textures. Because the LG C4 and PS5 Pro deliver such a sharp, clear picture, it actually makes the occasional low-resolution textures in main, highly trafficked areas stand out a bit more, briefly breaking the immersion. 

• Early Stability Issues: The game did hard crash on me during the very first mission's opening cutscene. Fortunately, performance was rock-solid after that initial hiccup with zero crashes since, but it’s worth noting for launch-week stability.

Final Thoughts: Minor texture seams and a singular day-one crash can't derail what is ultimately a masterpiece. If you have the hardware to push it to its limits, it's a visual treat, but even baseline, the gameplay makes you truly feel like Bond. This is an absolute must-play.

First Light delivers an exceptional origins story of a young, reckless James Bond brought to life with hearty charm by Patrick Gibson in a sleek, action-packed tale of identity, artificial intelligence, and conspiracy that puts many a silver screen outings to shame. Some rough spots come from trying to squeeze in as much Bond goodness as possible, but it’s hard to hold it against the game too much. Overall, First Light is a cinematic but engaging action-adventure game that balances player control with bombastic spectacle, proving IO Interactive were very much the right choice to break the pall that has lingered over the franchise’s gaming exploits over the last decade.

So, from at least me, I’d say IO Interactive’s license to continue killing it with instalments is more than granted…just don’t make the experience so bumpy with as many parts as Hitman, please?

I'm giving 007 First Light a light 7/10. My main enjoyment came from the story, which kept me engaged throughout the game. However, almost everything else felt fairly mediocre.

The open-area exploration, clearly inspired by the recent Hitman games, feels underdeveloped. Most objectives boil down to "go here, press a button, then go somewhere else and press another button." There are very few opportunities for players to creatively use their gadgets or approach situations in their own way, which is disappointing for a game centered around a spy like James Bond.

The melee combat is particularly rough. It often feels janky and unresponsive, and enemies can attack so quickly that countering them becomes frustrating rather than rewarding. Gunplay is serviceable, but nothing special; it gets the job done without ever standing out.

Overall, while the story provides a solid reason to see the game through to the end, the gameplay lacks the depth and polish needed to make 007 First Light truly memorable.

Also, their checkpoint system seems to be messed up when you try to return to a checkpoint; it goes back to a completely different checkpoint instead of being in the current area you are in

The name’s Bond. James Bond.

When this game was first announced in 2020, I wouldn’t even know what to really expect from this game, except all I knew that I knew it was going to be an awesome experience coming from one of my other favorite developers of all time, IO Interactive (shortened as IOI), known their groundbreaking and innovative assassination sandbox that is the Hitman franchise.

After a long 5 1/2 year development cycle, and with an ambitious scope after developing one of my favorite games of all time, Hitman 3, the question was that is this game that people would hoping it would be like Hitman meeting some bits of Uncharted?Well, I can immediately say that this game immediately brought back the legacy of Bond and delivered a fantastic first adventure with the iconic spy agent from start to finish.Really fantastic combat, that gives me Arkham and classic Yakuza vibes, gunplay that is reminiscent of Uncharted, story’s very strong, really well acted, pretty cool stealth mechanics that’s easier than Hitman, and despite some frame rate hiccups, a bit of a slower pacing, and some annoying sections while in combat, First Light feels like the start of something big that IOI is building up to and absolutely delivered on what it sets out to do.

Gibson’s portrayal of the iconic Bond is fantastic and the animation in the facial expressions and environment is really impressive and unreal to look at, and this game is a reminder that the Glacier engine is one impressive piece of technology and continues to get better and better with more titles from IOI.

007 First Light, is nearly perfect. It’s an awesome first time experience for IOI’s take on Bond and captured the essence of what makes 007 a pretty cool and fun experience for spy enthusiasts all around the world. This game to me gets a 9.5 out of 10. Truly an awesome first time and next step for IOI as both a developer and for their 007 games going forward. Super good.

items.quote: Pur presentando un intreccio tutto sommato interessante e avvincente, seppur fin troppo reiterato nel genere spy-action, First Light pecca decisamente dal punto di vista tecnico e di gameplay. Nel primo caso, in modalità prestazioni, la qualità delle textures è ormai di almeno cinque anni fa, con una grana pellicola fin troppo densa, atta a mascherare l'arretratezza delle textures, analogamente alle animazioni dei **** (incluse le animazioni facciali), ancorate oramai alla generazione precedente di console che, in tale ottica, non può assolutamente giustificare i cali di frame nelle situazioni più concitate o con un numero elevato di NPC, specie tenendo presente la natura lineare del gioco. Dal punto di vista del gameplay, il gioco si pone quale compromesso tra Hitman, prodotto della stessa software house di 007 e Uncharted, non riuscendo a raggiungere, purtroppo, i picchi di nessuno dei due: le possibilità di accesso sono molto più limitate rispetto a quelle dell'Agente 47, limitandosi il più delle volte a distrarre alcuni NPC e raccogliere chiavi d'accesso, ecc... con uno stealth estremamente inquadrato e fondato sul distrarre l'arretrata IA la quale, durante le fasi di shooting, appare più che predisposta a ricevere un headshot, risultando quindi affine a quella di Hitman, tollerabile per quest'ultima tipologia di gioco, ma non per un action. Infine, il prodotto soffre di gravi problemi di ritmo e ripetitività, dato che ciascuna missione è schematizzabile in: briefing, individuare la modalità d'accesso all'area protetta, fase stealth di infiltrazione, cutscene con il villain di turno, eventuale bossfight e fase di shooting con una pletora di sagome da poligono di tiro. In sostanza, si tratta di un prodotto nella media, che non innova nulla nel suo genere e che ripropone dinamiche consolidate ormai da almeno dieci anni, non riuscendo a proporre un comparto tecnico all'altezza di giochi in terza persona e lineari, anche non attuali

items.quote: It would have made for a perfect James Bond movie. The game perfectly captured every element of a James Bond film. I found the characters, in particular, to be very fitting. The Bond Girls were perfectly designed, and I was also very fond of the protagonist. What made the characters feel even more alive was the excellent facial motion capture; every subtle facial expression was captured, resulting in much more expressive dialogue and cutscenes. Both the dialogue and the narrative choices were solid—mostly quite humorous, though that didn't bother me at all. Next, we come to the game's greatest strength: its atmosphere and locations. It truly felt like watching several James Bond movies back-to-back. The range of settings was incredibly diverse, spanning everywhere from Vietnam to England. Exploring these locations was particularly enjoyable, though it did occasionally feel a bit repetitive. The balance between action and exploration was very well-executed. Quick Time Events (QTEs) appeared more frequently during the early stages of the game than they did later on; it would have been cool if that intensity hadn't tapered off. The infiltration mechanics also became somewhat repetitive, but the parkour and climbing sequences helped redeem those repetitive moments to some extent. In general, I really enjoyed the climbing mechanics—they felt very smooth. Speaking of smooth, both the HUD and the overall gameplay felt incredibly fluid. The combat reminded me of *Sifu* (in fact, the controls were even partially identical). The gunplay was also very satisfying, though I found myself running out of ammo quite quickly, which forced me to pause the gunplay briefly while I scrambled to pick up a new weapon. In terms of both combat and exploration, the gadgets were pretty cool—though I ended up using the laser and the dart gun most frequently.A few of the boss fights could have been designed a bit better, and I found the online system to be rather annoying. On a lighter note, the trophy names were pretty cool—they were all references to the titles of the James Bond films! My final point would be the game's performance. I experienced virtually no frame drops, except in the world section. And the ray tracing almost knocked my socks off—it was practically perfect.
items.author: chrolloprudo7

items.quote: This might be one of the best action adventure games I've ever played. A straight 10/10 experience from beginning to end. 007 First Light doesn't just capture what makes James Bond special, it fully embraces it and delivers the ultimate interactive Bond fantasy. From the opening mission to the final credits, I felt like I was starring in my own blockbuster spy film. The gameplay is where this game truly shines. The developers somehow managed to combine the best elements of Hitman and Uncharted into one seamless experience. On one hand, you have the freedom and creativity of a spy thriller where planning, infiltration, and stealth are rewarded. On the other hand, you have the cinematic set pieces, action sequences, and thrilling escapes that make every mission feel like it belongs in a Bond movie. What I loved most was the freedom of choice. Nearly every situation allows you to decide how you want to approach it. You can sneak through an area unnoticed, carefully taking down enemies and gathering intelligence. You can go in guns blazing and rely on your shooting skills to survive. Or you can mix both approaches together depending on how the mission unfolds. The game never forces you into a single playstyle, and that flexibility makes every mission feel exciting and replayable. The combat and fighting mechanics are also fantastic. Whether you're exchanging gunfire, engaging in hand to hand combat, or improvising during intense encounters, everything feels fluid and satisfying. The melee combat especially stood out to me because it feels impactful and cinematic without becoming repetitive. Every fight feels like something straight out of a James Bond film. The presentation is absolutely top tier. The visuals are stunning, the locations are breathtaking, and every mission feels larger than life. From glamorous high society events to dangerous enemy strongholds, the game constantly puts you in iconic Bond situations. The attention to detail is incredible, and the world feels authentic from beginning to end. The story is exactly what I wanted from a James Bond game. It delivers espionage, action, intrigue, betrayal, and memorable characters while maintaining the sophisticated charm that defines the franchise. It strikes the perfect balance between being a thrilling spy adventure and a personal journey for Bond himself. And I have to give special recognition to Lana Del Rey because she absolutely nailed the theme song. Her voice perfectly captures the elegance, mystery, and emotion that have always defined the best Bond themes. The song instantly felt iconic, and honestly, I'd love to hear her contribute to more movies in the future because she was the perfect choice for this soundtrack. What impressed me most is how cinematic the entire experience feels. Every mission, every action sequence, every conversation, and every set piece feels like you're playing through a major Hollywood production. It never loses sight of what makes James Bond special, and because of that, it succeeds on every level. It's rare for a game to perfectly blend action, stealth, storytelling, freedom of choice, and cinematic presentation, but 007 First Light somehow accomplishes all of it. For me, this isn't just a great James Bond game, it's one of the best action adventure games ever made.

items.quote: 007 First Light is easily one of the best James Bond games Ive played. It does a fantastic job of making you feel like a spy while still delivering satisfying action throughout the entire campaign. The biggest highlight for me was the combat, especially the melee combat. Every fight feels smooth, fluid & responsive, and taking down enemies up close never gets old & as for the gunplay, it's still good, but like most shooting games on a controller. The mission design is also excellent. Many objectives can be completed in different ways, whether through stealth, gadgets, or direct action, which gives players a lot of freedom in how they approach situations. The characters are another strong point. I found many of them memorable, and they helped keep me invested in the story from beginning to end. Visually, the game is also impressive, featuring a great variety of locations, from open outdoor areas and laboratories to office buildings and snowy mountain environments. The constant change in scenery keeps the adventure feeling fresh. My main complaint is that the game is too short. I also found the game surprisingly easy, even on Purist difficulty. Because enemies rarely pose much of a threat, I often found myself brute-forcing encounters instead of fully utilizing the gadget system. The gadgets are fun, but the lack of challenge means there's not always a strong reason to use them. Despite those issues, 007 First Light is an excellent spy action game with great combat, strong mission variety, memorable characters, and fantastic environments. I only wish it were longer and more challenging.

items.quote:
This game is an absolute masterpiece. The gameplay, the story, the pacing—it’s all just spot on. It completely nails the James Bond vibe; you truly feel like you are 007. I was entirely immersed for the roughly 15 hours it took me to complete the main story without doing tacsim, and I haven't had this much fun with a game in a very long time. I’m already looking forward to playing it again.

The way the social stealth blends with the action is brilliant. It feels like Uncharted married Hitman and had a child. The combat and shooting feel fantastic—never frustratingly hard, but never too easy either.

If you're looking for downsides, there are very few. I ran into a couple of bugs that required a reload, and the graphics might not be quite on par with the absolute best-looking titles on the market, but it gets close. Honestly, those are minor nitpicks.

I will be recommending this game to everyone. I truly hope it gets the massive success it deserves because the developers knocked it out of the park.

Thank you for three nights of undeniable fun, IO Interactive!

items.quote:
007 First Light is a game of contradictions. On a surface level, it's a very passable action game that pays good tribute to the source material, keeping the narrative flowing and not overstaying its' welcome. 

On the flipside, it's overly streamlined, extremely easy even on the hardest difficulty settings, has absolutely woeful driving segments and stilted combat.

It feels like a movie that reluctantly has gameplay sections. It's by no means bad, I enjoyed it, but the critic scores are clearly over the top - but then critics enjoying a game you need zero skill to play isn't exactly a new phenomenon.

My advice would be to wait for a sale and treat it like you would a rental game back in the day - good for one playthrough, something you won't regret playing but you'll forget about soon enough.

items.quote:
Mutch like the relic that is the James bond franchise, io interactives sterling effort feels like game design from the past often coming off like a "true crime" meets "stranglehold" meets "sleeping dogs" and even some of the jankiness of "enter the matrix". Wheras the latter carried the charm of being entirely new ip carving its own path in a dead sea of mario , GTA 3  and cod clones this outing carries the burden of high expectations often framed by talking heads as being an uncharted like AAA single player powerhouse. 

This is not what I found. Greetings to glitching ai that aften causes guards in fully rendered tac gear only to be seen walking into walls going nowhere or sitting on invisible chairs. Add in a generic forgettable plot about ai.Generic sounding underwhelming bond casting/accent/choice for a younger aged bond.Frustrating game design that doesn't feel as open as hitman or as "free flowing linear" as uncharted.Terrible driving sections feel awful too. Constant on screen interruptions saying "cannot connect to online server" even though it's a single player game. Non sensical resource system has your cinematic hero scrounging for washing conditioners and phone batteries to enable shoot a laser or knockout dart? Very long load times ps5 pro. Overused trope where character constantly knocked out only to load into cutaways for next gameplay/cut scene must've happened at least 25+ times across the play through no joke. 

Minute long unskippable title cards/safety notices etc each time you boot the game from dashboard. Distracting (almost) last gen like screen space based lighting artifacts are constantly distracting the eye.Poor HDR implementation results in less contrast than it should. Soft looking final image in spite of using 5 pro pssr2. Distracting near constant texture/lod swapping near player view. No manual save, checkpoint system seems random sporadic often had to replay the previous 15+mins gameplay as punishment when I chose"restart checkpoint" was just trying to listen to an alternative dialogue option I had selected by mistake. 

Positives now and witty banter can be very fun. Some of the combat sequences played out well with the explosive sections of scenery to create excitement. Overall thoughts so far are it's a good effort that comes across like a lesser hitman game with some uncharted esque influences that are poorly executed when you compare to uc4. 

I enjoyed io interactives good effort here and if you're on the fence, might be worth purchasing once it's found it's way to the bargain bin but I couldn't justify the current price to you outside of sheer enthusiasm that this is what you might want to try. Hopefully the tech issues I found will be patched over the games lifespan.

items.quote:
Incredible James Bond, best of the series by far. Starting from story, all the way to the combat. Other than usual day one issues like some minor glitches or game crashes, I haven't encountered any larger issues that can be seen with a lot of other games in recent times.

With game being built on Glacier engine (same one that powers Hitman World of Assassination, as well as older version powers Kane & Lynch) has once more proven to be powerful and equally open engine. By combining stealth elements from Hitman (although changed and adapted to this genre) as well as their knowledge of how to make a combat game from times of Kane & Lynch  (and well from the ever so disliked Hitman Absolution) has been combined into making this game as perfect as is. Some will say quite the opposite from me, but getting a game as polished, prepared and ready for release in 2026 is a hard job and a rare sight at that.

Going over to more "creative" part of the game, voice acting. Voice acting is superb, accents fit all the characters (looking at Hitman with limited accents as to oppose this one) as well as surprisingly large variance of voices for NPCs (looking at you Watch Dogs Legion), as well as amazing voice acting even for the lesser side characters like Monroe and Cressida.

At side of mechanics, I was concerned how that would play out and I must say I was shocked. From incredibly well thought-out hand-to-hand combat, gun play and the Q-watch mechanics have made me feel like I was James Bond and I was in the game. Q-watch was integrated in game with such detail that some parts of the game are near impossible to finish without it and it's not just a fun gimmick, and they managed to make it not feel like it's being stuck down your throat at that.

Yes, the game is linear, but so are their previous levels from previous IO games. The game features a robust replay menu, being able to start from nearly any point in the mission or just from the beginning and that adds extra layer of the openness to the game. Following in footsteps of Hitman once more, each level has at least half dozen different ways to reach the target location or accomplish a certain goal, offering hours of replayability and that certain feel of "branching linearity". Personally I feel that an open-world James Bond game would not work, James Bond isn't the type of person to run from point A to point B to grab certain things and missions, his missions are always time sensitive and have clear goals.

Considering the length of game at around 15 hours, some criticise it for being too short, however I believe in quality over quantity. As seen in some recent games with longer playtime, the added playtime just amounts to filler content that would make replaying the game tedious or just downright difficult at time.

Overall, it is my opinion that is going to be one of, if not the best game of 2026 (only game that could possibly top it is upcoming GTA VI, but that would be more of size) and it is incredible to see that a medium sized Danish developer that was in crisis in 2018 following loss of their partnership with Square Enix, come back even stronger and release the best Bond game of all time, and all that with "only" 200 million dollars of game budget.

items.quote:
Wow, wow!
Après environ 8 heures de jeu, je peux déjà dire une chose : James Bond: First Light est un gros potentiel GOTY 2026.

L'histoire est complètement nouvelle, repensée. Comme dans les films de James Bond, il y a plein de mystères, de twists et de rebondissements. Honnêtement, je suis tellement impressioné par le gameplay que j'en oubli que ce sont les créateurs des Hitmans qui l'ont fait. ( Hitman c'est bien, mais très clunky niveau contrôles.)

Côté gameplay, c'est probablement ce qui m'impressionne le plus. J'ai vraiment l'impression de jouer à un mélange entre Hitman et Uncharted. Tu peux être discret, infiltrer des endroits, utiliser des gadgets, puis quelques minutes plus **** te retrouver dans une grosse séquence d'action digne d'un film.

Pour les graphismes, je joue sur un PC haut de gamme avec une très bonne télé. Est-ce que ce sont les plus beaux graphismes que j'ai vus cette année? Non. Mais est-ce que c'est beau? Absolument. Les environnements sont détaillés, les personnages sont bien faits et tout roule super bien. Je donnerais facilement un 7.5/10 aux graphismes.

Là où le jeu frappe vraiment fort, c'est au niveau de l'ambiance. La musique, la mise en scène, les dialogues... tout te donne l'impression d'être James Bond. Pas juste de contrôler un personnage dans un jeu vidéo, mais vraiment d'incarner un jeune 007 à en devenir. C'est probablement ce que le jeu réussit le mieux. Un arrogance charmante, un trouble de l'opposition classique chez Bond. On a la chance d'incarner un gars de 26 ans qui malgré lui n'a aucune idée de la carrière et les challenges qui se préparent.

Patrick Gibson incarne avec brio le jeune James. J'avais deja trippé sur son jeu en tant que jeune Dexter dans la télé-série. Il est parfaitement à sa place et les personnages secondaires sont tous intéressants. Après seulement quelques heures t'es déjà attaché à eux.

Le plus gros compliment que je peux faire au jeu, c'est que je viens à peine de le commencer et je suis déjà un peu triste de savoir qu'il va finir dans un douzaine d'heures.(campagne de 20 heures environ.)

Ça fait longtemps qu'un jeu ne m'avait pas donné ce feeling-là. J'ai déjà hâte à une suite.

Pour moi, c'est un solide 9,5/10 jusqu'à présent. Une expérience vraiment incroyable et facilement une de mes plus belles surprises de l'année, parce que disons le, les previews étaient très , très moyens.

items.quote:
007 First Light had immense potential. 
Exploring the origins of entertainment's most famous secret agent, backed by today's technology, should have been an absolute triumph for the gaming industry. Instead, we are looking at yet another major casualty of a sterile, destructive contemporary trend. It is a forced reimagining that, in its clumsy attempt to pander to damaging and pointless modern hypersensitivities, ends up irreparably disfiguring and compromising a legendary character, and the statements made by the production team were sadly prophetic. At the end of the day, they feel like a slap in the face to anyone who actually knows and loves the franchise. Claiming that an "old school" James Bond is "tone deaf in this day" and masking the systematic dismantling of the character behind the rhetoric of "reflecting modern values" is an exercise in pure authorial arrogance. Associating "old school" with something negative is just absurd. They promise fans that the agent will retain his seductive charm, reassuring the audience that "beautiful women are there" (thank god, at least there is that) and that Bond "has got game", but it is all just a facade.Beneath the surface, the result is a sanitized and entirely flat protagonist filtered through the lens of ideological conformity, an approach that devolves into ridiculous, pointless, and harmful moralizing, stripping the game of its edge rather than adding any real depth. The pretentious question of "what does it take to save the world in 2026?" to justify stripping away the character's defining traits is not evolution: it is simply capitulating to a restrictive mindset.This title is the perfect embodiment of a broader sickness, a trend that is systematically ruining the entertainment world in all its forms, and gaming is no exception. The problem plaguing the industry, which First Light captures perfectly, is twofold. On one hand, you have major studios stubbornly failing to grasp, or worse, deliberately ignoring reality: the overwhelming majority of the audience simply wants to enjoy a work of fiction for what it is. Gamers are looking for escapism and immersion, and they want to be represented by strong characters who stay true to their core nature, without being subjected to constant moral lecturing or having historic icons clumsily rewritten just to avoid offending anyone (and honestly, who is even getting "offended" and by what?). Only when industry executives finally realize that normalcy and the actual demands of the market lie elsewhere, will we go back to getting products with genuine narrative integrity. On the other hand, there is a bitter truth regarding the audience itself: a significant portion of the player base passively accepts these shifts, consuming products with zero critical thinking or completely ignoring the bigger picture. It is exactly this lazy compliance that allows companies to get away with these approaches, validating the destruction of historic franchises. Making matters even more bitter is the technical side of things. And here lies another massive regret, because the graphics in 007 First Light are genuinely beautiful, finally looking good and fully worthy of the PlayStation 5. While not a flawless masterpiece, it is the only aspect of the game where the word "modern" actually makes sense to use. Despite that vocal minority of critics and players who stubbornly downplay the importance of visuals, proving they do not understand what technology, realism, and immersion truly mean in modern gaming, the graphics here prove to be absolutely fundamental. It is just a shame that the developers wasted such an impressive visual engine to deliver such a compromised creative vision, proving they should have focused their mental energy entirely on the technical execution, leaving the soul of James Bond well enough alone.

items.quote: 007 First Light is a triumphant return for the James Bond franchise, delivering the definitive modern spy experience. Shifting the focus to a gripping origin story, the game successfully carves out its own unique identity. The gameplay is a brilliant blend of IO Interactive’s signature stealth mechanics, precise gunplay, and blockbuster action set-pieces. From Iceland to Malta, the level design strikes a perfect balance between open-ended tactical freedom and a tight, cinematic narrative. Visually, the game is stunning, boasting incredible attention to detail and flawless performance. Bond’s iconic dry wit is perfectly captured in the writing, making the character feel both fresh and familiar. While it trades a bit of the pure sandbox freedom found in the Hitman series for a more structured story, the pacing never falters. Ultimately, 007 First Light is a polished, stylish, and immensely fun masterclass in game design. It is an absolute must-play for both action-stealth fans and Bond enthusiasts alike.

HOWEVER, the gameplay was atrocious, the fighting and shooting were really bad, i feel like they definitely rushed it a lot to make the release date, this game definitely needed a few more months in development for polishing, the stealth was also pretty bad, the devs who are responsible for the Hitman series couldn't include the ability to move bodies and add disguises? seems like a pretty bad choice not to include those very basic things for stealth gameplay with is also lacklustre, on the initial intro mission i broke into unit A9 i believe it was? anyway i dropped down from the roof onto an enemy, there were no other enemies around in sight or near by in general, but upon taking him down the entire camp was notified of his death, this proceeded to continue throughout the game, i'd take down an enemy with no one around but surrounding enemies were still notified. i really enjoyed the story and characters although the poor gameplay held the game back significantly, i hope for a sequel where the gameplay is ****'s also very clear that 007 first light steals a lot from other games, Combat is clearly from TLOU, Stealth and the Stealth Takedowns take a lot from Uncharted, there is even a mission set in a basement that is EXACTLY like the fight between Abby and Ellie in the basement of the theatre, this game is really uninspiring, and a total mess, with server issues popping up every hour telling me i've lost connection to their servers, this was supposed to be my personal 2026 GOTY, but i don't think it even deserves a slot in my top 5. driving mechanics are outdated and stiff and clunky, loading times are awful as well, you die or fail you'll be waiting on a black screen for a good few seconds.

items.quote:
As you can see I do not often review but I felt I had to this time, not long after you take your first tentative steps into First Light, when it becomes absolutely clear that IO Interactive has not merely made a good James Bond game. They have made the definitive James Bond game. Possibly the best Bond experience in any medium since the franchise's golden era.

The premise is inspired. This is an original origin story, following a 26-year-old James Bond, a promising but occasionally reckless Royal Navy air crewman who catches the attention of MI6 and finds himself recruited into the newly revived 00 programme. It sounds straightforward on paper, but the execution is anything but. The story that unfolds from that foundation is layered, surprising, and genuinely gripping from beginning to end.Patrick Gibson is an absolute revelation in the lead role. He has the considerable advantage of a twenty-hour game rather than just two hours of film to develop the character, and he uses every minute of it. 

This is a Bond who feels real, flawed, charming, and worth caring about. He earns the number. You believe every step of the way, gameplay is where IO Interactive truly flex their craft. Their years building the Hitman franchise have prepared them perfectly for this moment. The stealth systems are deep and satisfying, but what sets this apart is how it wraps all of that in unmistakable Bond DNA. This is not a cold, clinical assassin. This is a charismatic spy who talks his way into restricted areas, improvises under pressure, and always manages to look good doing it. The social stealth missions in particular are some of the finest levels in recent gaming memory, with enormous sandboxes and an almost overwhelming number of ways to approach any given objective. You can play it loud, or you can play it smart, and both feel completely valid, supporting cast gives the whole production genuine cinematic weight, and the production values throughout are frankly staggering. This looks and feels like a Bond film that just happens to also be interactive. 

Then there is the theme song. Lana Del Rey has finally got her Bond song, and she has made it count. Co-written and composed with the legendary David Arnold, "First Light" is a slow burner that reveals its full emotional depth only as you settle into the world of the game. When it swells across that title sequence, it stops you cold. It is elegant, atmospheric, and unmistakably Bond, the kind of track that sits comfortably alongside the very best the franchise has ever produced. It was worth the wait. After fourteen years without a Bond game worthy of the name, IO Interactive has delivered something genuinely extraordinary. This is the game Bond fans have been waiting for. A love letter to the franchise, a triumph of game design, and frankly one of the most enjoyable experiences you will have in front of a screen this year. Do not miss it.

items.quote:
First release I preordered in a while. And never regretted it in the 12h I played through the main campaign. 

Gameplaywise, the IOI formula of levels being a completely open Sandbox is working perfectly in tandem with the toys you get. You WILL know the basics of a load of those if you played Hitman but/and the Bluffing is a decent mechanic to add to that toolbox. The limit in Insinct, Chemicals and Electricity may seem too strict at the very first, but the more you get the hand of the gadgets and mechanics, the more naturally you'll flow between them and with little time you'll have organically developed your own kind of "Attack Flow". And all of that perfectly immerses you into the story it wants to tell if you let it.

The characters are nice, especially the Bond. Patrick Gibson really nailed the role. I dont want to spoiler it tho.

Technic side is the only -1 for me. I played on a regular PS5 using Performance Mode. I did encounter some low detail textures not loading into high res, but those were rather rare. The more pressing ones are one full game crash, rather sparingly set Checkpoints in a game that cannot be manually saved (or I was too dumb to find the button) and, by far the worst of all, a couple of server disconnects. The latter being a huge annoyance and if you know how they handled that in Hitman or how Square Enix did it in JC3, you know why but if you dont... wherever you are or whatever you're doing, once the servers are lost, the game gets forced into a pause and will remain on full hold until the complete reconnect is done. That should be moved into the background of things. The servers are not that important. Doing automatic background reconnects should very much be possible and would greatly increase the experience overall.

items.quote:
I’ve been a long term Hitman player & fan.

It is simply a technical marvel. Years of massive work were put into the game, and I can see the complexity and details at every step. The programming of the AI, vehicles, water, interactive objects and situations — must have been insanely complex, considering the driving mechanics simply lacked in Hitman. The story is massive and takes hours to complete (it really does feel like progressing through a movie — but you’re the main character), but overall it is worth it — and it is well written and the action is fast-paced. The culturally diverse backgrounds, the presence of multiple languages — including the details of levels, the reactions of NPCs, even the dried rain stains on glass or the design of the euro banknotes or the electrocution of NPCs — all overwhelmingly accurate — is what did it for me. I loved the Finnish brothers part. Honestly, my family thought that it’s a movie at first. Easily one of the best games in the year 2026 and beyond — no other James Bond game has ever reached this level. Bravo, IOI. I sure do hope the next Hitman games or other IPs will adopt these mechanics. I’m honestly surprised all NPCs react to you bumping into them — it only makes the world more realistic, alive and complex. 

Lastly, I love that enemy NPCs now know how to flank you. Yes — they flanked me hard and formed a perimeter and I died. Scandalous. They also draw weapons in rare, contextual/special cases which makes it even more realistic — it gives you a window to fight until chaos ensues.

P.S. Romanian subtitles missing were me doing the hard work of translating British puns and charming lines to my brother. After all, I paid the full price and pre-ordered it — to catch up on my English class. And yes, I went with hard mode — so reloading checkpoints basically became my favorite task.

items.quote: I honestly didnt expect this game to hit me THIS hard.I waited for this game for months because I love James Bond movies, especially Daniel Craig era, and somehow this game actually made me FEEL like Bond more then some of the movies themselves.This is not just "another action game". The whole vibe is insane. From the intro, the music, the MI6 base, gadgets, betrayals, conspiracies, missions, all of it just works together perfectly. There were multiple moments where I literally sat there thinking "holy **** this is exactly what I wanted from a Bond game".What surprised me most is how cinematic everything feels. The game reminds me of Uncharted sometimes with the huge setpieces and pacing, but also Hitman with stealth and freedom in missions. But it still has its own identity. It doesnt feel like a copy.I LOVE how the game slowly builds Bond into the legend instead of making him a perfect super agent from the start. The whole beginning with training and becoming the last surviving 00 agent actually made me care about the story and character way more then I expected.Also one thing that I absolutely loved:you are not just running around shooting everyone. The game actually makes you feel like an AGENT. Sometimes you cant even use your gun until things go completely wrong and someone pulls a weapon first. Then suddenly you get that "license to kill" feeling and the gameplay changes completely. Its so damn **** honestly? The story got me hard. The feeling that MI6 basically leaves you alone, that you are outside the system trying to uncover a huge conspiracy while only a few people still trust you... thats PEAK James Bond for me. It felt exactly like those Daniel Craig movies where Bond always ends up isolated and has to fix everything himself.I played around 20 hours total because I didnt want to rush it. I literally stopped before the ending because I had work in 2 hours and I didnt want to experience the finale tired or half focused. Thats how much I cared about this game by the end.Only negatives for me:car crash/chase sequences felt weaker then the rest of the gameplay and I wish weapon customization was deeper, especially suppressors because its Bond after **** yeah, I understand why some people think 70 dollars/euros is expensive. It IS expensive. But I also think people forget inflation exists. Just because AAA games cost 60 dollars 10 years ago doesnt mean they can realistically stay the same forever while budgets become insane.Back then many huge games cost like 20-30 million to make. Now games like this use full performance capture, hollywood level cinematics, massive teams, licensed IPs and budgets that can hit 200-300 million dollars. People say they want big cinematic singleplayer games and sequels, but at the same time dont want these games to actually make enough money to survive and get future parts.Honestly I would rather pay 70 for a polished memorable experience like this then spend 100 hours in some bloated boring open world full of filler **** Interactive seriously cooked with this one. Please let this game sell well because I NEED a sequel.
